The nucleation exponent is evaluated through both WKB wall penetration and a Brown–Teitelboim Euclidean bounce. Extremising the bounce action reproduces the Israel junction condition; its large-curvature-scale expansion is compared with the four-dimensional exponent.

Cross-correlate reconstructed φ̃=βφ with a large-scale-structure mass tracer m. In the small-angle forecast, σ(β)⁻²≈f_skyΣ_L(2L+1)ρ_L²C_L^{φφ}/N_L^{φ̃φ̃}. The reconstruction combines EB and BB inverse noise; comparison forecasts use the EB-spectrum Fisher information.

Test reconstruction with full-sky Gaussian primary-CMB and lensing-potential simulations, remapping followed by a 1° rotation. The example uses 5 μK-arcmin polarization noise, temperature noise lower by √2, and a 1-arcmin Gaussian beam; the displayed cross-spectrum averages 100 realizations.

Expand distorted CMB fields in spherical harmonics to first order in distortion fields, derive covariance kernels including parity-odd spectra, and insert the new kernels into normalized inverse-variance-weighted quadratic estimators.

Constructs the four-dimensional supergravity scalar potential from the Kähler potential, flux and nonperturbative superpotentials, leading α′ correction and brane energy. Uses large-volume/small-deformation expansions, analytic critical-point estimates, field-metric-weighted mass matrices and numerical solutions of the retained full potential.
Separate a boundary logarithm from a convergent warp correction. Use consistent radial functions, controlled matching, and a separately verified integral value; 0.093 remains a source-reported input.
Evaluate weighted differential-form pairings and normalize by the background integral. The paper reviews this operation for one KS deformation; bulk dominance is a subsequent approximation.

Reviews dimensional reduction and the warped complex-structure metric computed from weighted three-form integrals. The appendix uses radial integration by parts, a throat-to-bulk cutoff and bulk dominance to obtain the logarithmic and warp-dependent contributions.
Count levels with m_n≲ε, multiply by an assumed common integrated energy and invert energy equality. This operation requires a uniform energy estimate absent here.
Hold geometry and mass history fixed, solve Fourier oscillators, and compare instantaneous ground states. This isolates mass-driven production from curvature effects.
Define instantaneous Hamiltonian ground states, solve their basis transformation and interpret |β_k|² as occupation relative to the final reference vacuum.

CppTransport and PyTransport independently implement transport evolution, using slow roll only to initialize correlators. The primary search samples 450 million backgrounds; numerical cuts reduce roughly 90,000 inflationary trajectories to 55,000.

Where feasible, 100 logarithmically spaced scalar-spectrum samples over 10^-6–50 Mpc^-1 feed CLASS through CosmoSIS and the Planck2015 likelihood. Post-inflationary cosmological parameters remain fixed at historical Planck2015 best-fit values; some trajectories lack enough inflation for this likelihood calculation.

Potential construction uses Peter–Weyl harmonic analysis, Wigner matrices, a spectral Green function and Clebsch–Gordan decomposition of flux products. These mathematical ingredients are collected from earlier work.

Expand fermions in creation and annihilation operators and diagonalise the Hermitian mode-evolution matrix. Diagnose ultraviolet production through the high-momentum behaviour of the frequency-based non-adiabaticity coefficient Ak.

Derive the coupled θ–Υ quadratic system, rescale to canonical fields Ψ1, Ψ2, and express its kinetic and mass terms through mixing matrices N and M. The vector-multiplet case is brought to the same canonical structure as the two-chiral case.

Use a time-dependent unitary transformation to remove N, an orthogonal transformation L to remove the antisymmetric mass component, and an orthogonal matrix C to diagonalise the remaining real symmetric mass matrix. The connection Γ = Cᵀ∂0C enters the physical mode equations.

Expand the ADM action to quadratic order in comoving, uniform-field gauge and eliminate lapse/shift constraints. Canonically normalize scalar and tensor perturbations, impose Bunch-Davies boundary conditions, and obtain approximate Hankel-function mode solutions.

Select the real, positive Friedmann-cubic branch nonsingular as ξ → 0. Taylor-expand ξ around a fixed point and linearize the field-velocity dynamical system; classify local behavior through its eigenvalues.

Constrain a local cubic Taylor parametrization of ξ using spectral tilt, running and tensor-to-scalar ratio. Fix ξ̄₂ from the central spectral-index value at leading order, then examine ξ̄₁ and ξ̄₃ for specified initial displacements and velocities.

Analyze a three-current Green function with one global axial and two gauge currents. Track loop-momentum-routing ambiguities, impose gauge-current conservation, and separate the anomaly from the classical fermionic mass contribution and the axion contribution to the full nonlinear current.
Review fermion-triangle decay diagrams using Dirac traces, Bose exchange, Feynman parameters and an expansion in inverse fermion mass. Match the leading amplitude onto a local aFμνF̃μν interaction.

Insert the modulated scalar spectrum into the quadratic GW integral and separate terms of order Alog⁰, Alog¹ and Alog². Logarithm identities and trigonometric product identities factor out the k dependence; the remaining kernel integrals determine frequency-dependent amplitudes and phases.

A complementary peak-comb analysis applies the imported resonance-location rule kmax,ij=(k*i+k*j)/√3, subject to kmax,ij>|k*i−k*j|. The authors compare its predictions and their semi-analytic templates with numerical spectra.

Torus, Klein-bottle, cylinder and Möbius partition functions are compared in loop and transverse channels. Closed-string propagation phases, weighted by tensions and RR charges, reconstruct O-plane locations and momentum projectors.
The brane-position dependence of the one-loop potential is extracted from the Möbius amplitude. Energetic arguments and a numerical negative-gradient field support the preferred brane configuration.

Derive one- and two-loop β-functions through a doubled gradient flow using double field theory. The scheme choice incorporates deformed double Lorentz symmetry and generalized Green–Schwarz transformations.

Represent nilpotent elements using multi-pronged strings between [p,q] 7-branes, then condense junctions to track recombination and Higgsing. Compute 6D anomalies through one-loop contributions and Green–Schwarz square completion.

Use UV anomaly matching and a-maximization to determine candidate IR R-symmetries. Introduce emergent U(1) charges and repeat maximization when Coulomb operators or highest-spin chiral mesons violate the unitarity bound.

Use thermal-field-theory spectral functions and a numerical interpolation for Υ across the high- and low-temperature regimes. Numerically integrate the homogeneous inflaton-radiation equations to follow the end of inflation and transition to radiation domination.

Estimate PBH formation using Gaussian Press-Schechter statistics and a Gaussian smoothing window. Compute induced tensors through the radiation-era convolution of two scalar spectra and redshift the resulting GW energy density to today.

Integrate coupled inflaton, radiation and metric perturbations, including Gaussian quantum and thermal Langevin noises, in longitudinal shear-free gauge. Fit the growing-mode function using auxiliary quartic models with constant κ, then use direct numerical spectra near the end where that approximation fails.

Numerical overshoot–undershoot shooting uses η = R₃/R rather than the central scalar value. The action calculation includes both a center contribution and the potential integral relative to the false vacuum.

The authors formulate a Euclidean Coleman–De Luccia scalar-gravity boundary-value problem with bubble-of-nothing boundary conditions. The radion starts at φ = −∞ at the center, replacing the regular CDL condition φ′(0) = 0.

Analytic construction matches a rescaled Witten bubble onto a small-field massive-radion solution involving K₁(mρ)/(mρ), followed by the de Sitter exterior. Continuity of φ and φ′ determines the matching constants and bubble radius.

The central analysis identifies necessary ingredients of selection mechanisms rather than constructing detailed models. A previously proposed many-species hierarchy bound is used as an analogy for a hierarchy imposed by gravitational consistency.

A parametric consistency argument compares the gravitational scattering strength q²G with the limit required to make a finite-curvature de Sitter background rigid against scattering backreaction. The argument is explicitly imported from earlier work.

Integrating the FPV across a continuous-potential kink gives ΔP′/P = −2Δω′/α in EFT variables. Multibranch transitions instead use absorbing conditions on a terminating branch and matching conditions that transfer its flux to the surviving branch.

Analytic Airy-function solutions for linear and pyramid potentials illustrate localization and peak widths. A diffusionless approximation analyzes classical drift–volume balance and the waterfall construction.

The volume-weighted Fokker–Planck equation combines stochastic diffusion, classical drift, and volume growth. Spectral decomposition, positivity, and boundary conditions identify the largest-eigenvalue mode governing the asymptotic distribution.

Express the potential through flux–axion polynomials, solve algebraic vacuum equations, and use matrix rank, monodromy invariants and positive on-shell tadpole contributions to constrain stabilization.

Homological mirror symmetry identifies four-fold periods with B-brane central charges. Γ-class central charges and Todd-class open-string indices organize polynomial curvature corrections and corrected flux pairings.

Use a worldline action with field-dependent mass m(φ), expand the radial effective potential at large distance, and match scalar coupling to black-hole charges. Tree-level scattering and two-dilaton emission amplitudes probe the resulting point-state model.

Classify zeros outside the singular surface using polynomial roots or intersections of a straight line and a curvature-dependent function. Horizon mergers satisfy F=F′=0; small-H expansions connect curved-space boundaries to flat-space ones.

Expand χ in curvature orders, solve recursive duality constraints by induction, and sum the even-order coefficients using the Taylor series of √(1+x²). This yields a tensor square-root expression for the full susceptibility.

Vary the symmetry-reduced Lagrangian to obtain metric and Maxwell equations. For extremality, apply Sen’s entropy-function method: evaluate on AdS₂×S², Legendre transform with respect to the electric field, and extremize over both radii and that field.

Interpret each winding contribution through a proper-time saddle and a relativistic worldline action including σ. Assess higher-derivative corrections using a perturbed dyon spectrum and a further saddle-point expansion.

Compute the one-loop vacuum energy either by summing Coleman-Weinberg-type contributions from dyon states or by a first-quantized Euclidean worldline path integral. Poisson resummation converts the dyon sum into a periodic winding expansion.
Multiterminal lock-in measurements use 200 nA AC current at 12.357 Hz; two-terminal measurements use 10 mV AC bias. Gate control tunes the Fermi energy through the insulating region.

Bulk/edge separation grounds contacts 1 and 5 while biasing contact 3 and measuring current at 7, intended to divert edge currents before they reach the meter. Nine 6-SL Hall bars of differing dimensions provide a separate channel-length/width diagnostic.

The calculation regularizes a nonmagnetic continuum model on a cubic lattice, adds alternating out-of-plane layer magnetization, and uses periodic x/open y boundaries with 6 or 7 layers along z. Wave-function distributions and eight-lead transmissions are calculated; Kwant and the Landauer–Büttiker formula give resistances.

Matched analytic approximations join a Witten-like core, a transition region, and the dS exterior. A piecewise constant/quadratic potential makes the transition tractable through modified Bessel functions; the vacuum-subtracted action retains the dimensional-reduction total derivative.

Numerical construction uses Runge–Kutta integration and overshoot–undershoot bisection. R5 is held fixed while η=R3/R5 is varied; small-ξ series, including potential-dependent corrections, supply sensitive initial data.
A conformal metric transformation and canonical field redefinition relate the frames. The displayed relations are VE=Mpl⁴VJ/F² and (dϕ/dφ)²=Z⁻¹, with Z⁻¹=Mpl²[1/F+(3/2)(d log F/dφ)²].

The author compares slow-roll parameters for constant and field-dependent coupling, expands in weak/strong coupling, and outlines an N=1, D=4 superconformal embedding using a generic F-term potential and modifications of the Kähler potential.

The authors complete squares, impose the flux equation and dG=0, and use Hodge decomposition to solve G=G(0)+2Pe(j), with harmonic quantized background G(0) and exact projection Pe. ISD/IASD decomposition isolates a local delta-function-squared divergence.

Intersection pairings Kij=∫X[Σi]∧[Σj]∧J motivate the finite subtraction. The diagonal pairing is rewritten using c1(O(Σ))=[Σ] and O(Σ)|Σ=N as Kii=∫ΣiF(Ni)∧J, making the finite contribution locally geometric.

Zero-mode decomposition Ψ=λ⊗χ, chirality and commuting-spinor Fierz identities relate the proposed 8d curvature operator to the self-intersection term. Dimensional reduction, Weyl rescaling, gaugino normalization and Kähler-metric identities then compare it with 4d supergravity.
Solve algebraic inequalities and inspect parameter contour plots for ns and r; subsequently evaluate V′/V, −V″/V, and, in selected models, the field excursion at horizon crossing.

Use leading-order Friedmann and scalar equations, impose slow roll, solve ε₁(φend) = 1, and determine the horizon-crossing field through N = (κ²/α)∫φend^φ V/V′ dφ. Several observable expressions are expanded in 1/N.

Introduce Gaussian damping away from the singularity to define asymptotic in/out vacua. Extract Bogoliubov coefficients through Wronskians, use a Born Fourier-transform estimate at large mode number, and supplement the divergent case with a junction-condition argument.
Use the Polyakov action in conformal gauge and light-cone gauge u = α′pτ. Transverse Fourier modes obey independent linear Schrödinger equations with energy n² and potential α′²p²A(α′pτ).

Take a Penrose limit around a null geodesic, transform Rosen coordinates to Brinkmann coordinates, and study ds² = −2du dV + A(u)(X² + Y²)du² + dX² + dY² instead of quantizing strings directly on FLRW.

An alternative derivation uses a moduli-space/upper-half-plane differential equation and modular uniqueness. Fourier expansions of Eisenstein series provide the explicit prime-level spectral analysis.

Extend Siegel averaging to two independent rational twists by decomposing lattice sums into residue classes, reducing to the imported single-twist theorem, and fixing cusp coefficients through modular transformations.
Decompose affine characters into string functions and theta functions, express twisted toroidal partition functions as Siegel-Narain theta functions, and average the lattice-dependent factor.

Shock geometries are studied using an infinite boost of a particle geometry and an explicit outgoing Vaidya shell. Matching the transverse circumference and pole time across the shell determines the near-horizon null-geodesic shift.

The paper imports Hayden–Preskill decoupling reasoning: information transfer is diagnosed by loss of correlations between the inaccessible subsystem and a reference system, with Haar-averaged unitary evolution motivating recovery after a few additional emitted qubits.

The stress-tensor calculation uses static/global mode expansions, Bogoliubov transformations, thermal tracing, UV subtraction, the conformal anomaly, and the Schwarzian contribution when changing null coordinates.
For the seed analysis, a quartic Kähler deformation fixes Re φ = b. Writing φ = x + iy then gives the effective canonical imaginary field σ = √(3α/2)y/b.
Authors evaluate covariant scalar Hessians with inverse Kähler-metric factors. At the selected rolling-model extrema, mixed no-scale/rolling components vanish, permitting separate Hessian blocks.

Construct the thermally corrected Higgs potential, including the SM-Higgs thermal mass from daisy resummation. Numerically evolve the homogeneous radial equation with a small initial kick to estimate the oscillation abundance and suppression factor Ceff.

Derive thermal dissipation using effective equations and a Hartree approximation for nearly monochromatic NG modes. An alternative optical-theorem estimate uses a thermal-width-resummed Higgs spectral density.

Estimate Bose-enhanced NG production from the resonance band, compare its growth with Hubble expansion and portal dissipation, and combine production and annihilation-limited yields to estimate the surviving abundance.

Solve and order lapse zeros, verify the static interval, perturb the roots, and translate the resulting size interval into a parameter bound. In this paper the lapse is Schwarzschild–de Sitter and the small parameter is GMH.

Convert a fluctuation time shift into a density increment using an assumed scale-factor response, integrate over the approximate horizon volume, and insert the resulting excess mass into the horizon comparison.

Differentiate a potential, infer a constant kinetic coefficient from a chosen tilt and field value, solve the inflation endpoint, and integrate the trajectory. The paper uses benchmarks because the endpoint also varies with potential parameters.

Coupled Boltzmann equations track inflaton energy, radiation energy, and dark-matter number density. During reheating the calculation uses N=na³ because SM entropy is being produced; after radiation domination it uses the yield Y=n/s.

Appendix A thermally averages an inflaton-mediated Breit–Wigner annihilation cross section using a modified Bessel function K1 and temperature-dependent approximations. Appendix B estimates a free-streaming constraint by redshifting the decay momentum and matching a present-day warm-dark-matter velocity bound.

The inflation analysis reviews slow-roll expansions near the inflection point using δ=1−φ/φ0. Analytic expressions relate the potential parameters to the number of e-folds, scalar amplitude, spectral index, running, and tensor-to-scalar ratio.

The spectral argument contrasts exponential decay required by a symmetry commutator with sums of discrete-frequency phases. Their nonzero late-time mean square obstructs decay to zero. Replacing the spectral sum by a continuum integral estimates how the obstruction scales with level spacing.

Fluctuation probabilities are estimated from conditional entropy deficits, PO=e^(−ΔS). General relativity supplies the horizon areas. Euclidean continuation and the Nariai saddle then connect a rare thermal fluctuation to a nonperturbative gravitational path-integral contribution.

A four-step diagnostic constructs a thermal static-patch system, doubles it into podal and antipodal copies, attempts to build the remaining de Sitter generators, and imposes their gauge constraints. The doubled Hamiltonian is H=Hp−Ha, and the de Sitter vacuum is represented by a thermofield-double state.

The field obeys the homogeneous Klein–Gordon equation φ̈+3Hφ̇+dV/dφ=0. Its endpoint displacement determines β=(gφγγ/2)(φ0−φ*). The letter uses previously reported mass requirements for this explanation rather than supplying a new birefringence-data likelihood analysis.

The authors expand the periodic gravitational potential to estimate its mass contribution, require that contribution to remain below the birefringence-compatible mass scale, and express the resulting suppression requirement as a logarithmic lower bound on SQG.
The D1 world-volume analysis uses one-loop functional determinants around separated-stack scalar configurations and a heat-kernel argument for gauge-coupling running.

Back-reacted geometries are studied through a constrained Toda-like radial system, integrable for p=8. Probe potentials follow from DBI-type tension terms and Wess–Zumino couplings evaluated on the backgrounds.

Large-separation string potentials are extracted from transverse-channel annulus asymptotics, with unspecified positive overall normalization. For q=7,8, divergent potential integrals receive a distributional treatment yielding finite forces.

Superconformal multiplet calculus constructs Weyl-squared and T-log invariants; gauge fixing and elimination using two-derivative on-shell superconformal fields give the physical action. Polynomial composite multiplets are organized by derivative counting.

Holographic renormalization combines two-derivative and Gauss–Bonnet boundary counterterms to regularize the Weyl-squared completion. Wald entropy, boundary-stress-tensor charges and Maxwell–Bianchi integrals determine thermodynamics; imported localization data fix holographic combinations.

Rotate the anomalous coupling into the quark mass matrix and match to a chiral Lagrangian. The small-angle potential is approximately Λ⁴(⟨h⟩)(θ+φ−/F−+φ+/F+)²/2, with Λ⁴=[mu md/(mu+md)²]mπ²fπ² for mu,d≲4πfπ.

Analyze local extrema, solve the classical scalar equations with Hubble friction, estimate traversal and crunching times, and estimate metastable-vacuum tunnelling and coherent-oscillation relic density.

Match Weyl-rescaled 3D M-theory and IIB Lagrangians, then count inverse base/fibre metrics in internal curvature–flux contractions. A schematic 11D one-loop analysis treats nonzero winding sectors for trivial fibrations.
Use classical rescaling weights, axionic shifts and the superconformal chiral compensator to constrain corrections to e^(−K/3). Count flux insertions to organize the higher-F-term expansion.
Integrate the Maxwell equation using conserved pA, then seek power laws α=ζ log t, σ=η log t, φ=ξ log t+φ0 and θ=γt^p+θ0 in the large-radius approximation.

Rewrite evolution as a dynamical system in Hubble-normalized variables using e-fold time. Classify fixed points, calculate Jacobian eigenvalues, and examine numerical trajectories and parameter flows.

Combines semi-analytic integration with numerical RG solutions using two-loop running of SM gauge and top Yukawa couplings. Heavy-particle matching connects UV parameters to light-quark/electron coefficients; pion mixing and lattice nucleon inputs then give observable couplings.

Develops leading Yukawa- and gauge-induced RG equations, extending Yukawa expressions to general 2HDMs and gauge expressions to SUSY using the relation between axion beta functions and chiral-superfield anomalous dimensions.

Integrates out gravitons coupled to a massless scalar in de Donder gauge, linearizes around a scalar-gradient background, and uses a low-energy spectral representation to study the sign of the effective kinetic correction.

Uses reported eikonal scattering and bending calculations, including unitarity-based graviton cuts, to connect nonanalytic momentum-space logarithms with spacetime nonlocality and species-dependent propagation.

Uses the in-in formalism with doubled fields and sources, Schwinger–Dyson equations for Wightman functions, and a large-distance contour argument for the Pauli–Jordan function. Merlin poles supply the proposed obstruction to spacelike commutator vanishing.

Monte Carlo pipeline: FeynRules/UFO, leading-order MadGraph5_aMC@NLO with NNPDF2.3QED, Pythia8 showering, Delphes fast detector simulation and FastJet. Energy-flow objects are clustered using anti-kt with R=0.4, retaining the leading jet. Generation cuts are pTj>20 GeV and |ηj|<5.

Each jet becomes a four-channel 40×40 image spanning [-0.4,0.4]² in relative η–φ, with 0.02×0.02 pixels. Channels sum transverse momentum for all particles, photons, charged hadrons and neutral hadrons. Translation, barycenter rotation and fixed rescaling precede a CNN with depthwise convolutions, channel/spatial attention and three-class SoftMax output; training uses cross-entropy, Adam and early stopping.

A second network takes the three tagging probabilities, uses a ten-neuron hidden layer and sigmoid selection output, and optimizes differentiable estimates of event yields. Seven selection-network trainings estimate significance variation; QCD samples are bootstrapped to 3 million events per training because surviving background tails are expensive to simulate.

The black-hole argument compares Schwinger discharge, schematically exp[−m²/(qE)], with slow evaporation and pathological rapid screening/crunching. Matching electric WGC extremality to a magnetic-monopole/Nariai argument gives g²≥(3/2)(H/MP)² and fixes a proposed four-dimensional FL coefficient; this is a consistency argument, not a direct strong-Schwinger calculation.

A proposed microscopic mechanism combines flux-vacuum decay by membranes, a worldvolume A∧F̃ coupling inducing particle charge, and brane polarization. The membrane-particle mass scaling contains an undetermined coupling exponent; its classical value gives a weaker relation than FL.

Extensions use summed or density-integrated Schwinger rates for charged towers and the charge quadratic form qAqB(f⁻¹)AB for multiple U(1)s. Dimensional reduction tracks Einstein-frame radion dependence, KK masses, gauge couplings and Casimir thresholds.

Represent vector condensation by a real spurion to extract soft scalar masses. For gravitational effects, integrate out A0 and analyze the quadratic longitudinal-vector/gravitational-potential system, then apply imported preferred-frame and black-hole-accretion constraints.

Construct higher-derivative actions in global SUSY superspace, eliminate the chiral auxiliary field on the F=0 branch, and analyze homogeneous P(X) solutions using the scalar equation and Friedmann equations. Quartic Kähler terms supply matter masses and stabilize the companion scalar χ.

For non-self-dual momentum lattices, use coroot and cocharacter lattices in the dual momentum lattice: π1(G)=M∨/L∨. Exploring the appropriately rescaled dual lattice and dualizing the resulting algebra handles non-ADE factors.

The exploration algorithm starts from an explicit maximal enhancement, removes a simple root, searches for alternative re-enhancements, and repeats until no new results appear. Global data are computed from lattice overlattices and their central-quotient generators.

Embed reduced-rank momentum lattices into the Narain lattice, identify their orthogonal complements, and compare primitive completions and root systems. This yields freezing rules and projection maps for the central subgroup defining the global quotient.

Times successive crossings of the positive x-axis. The principal detection observable is ΔTmax = max over i,j of |Ti − Tj| across a prescribed number of complete 2π revolutions, replacing comparison against an uncertain predicted Newtonian period.

Uses classical central-force equations in polar coordinates and scans source mass and initial conditions. Eccentricity is increased subject to boundedness and avoidance of collisions, comparing Newtonian and Yukawa trajectories.
Decomposes W = W0 + W1, with W0 linear in X and W1 at least quadratic in X and A. Setting X = A = 0 eliminates all F-terms except NX equations in Y and eligible neutral products P(r)Q(−r).

Supports the construction with analytic examples and numerical solutions for a degenerate-charge example. The latter has three reduced equations in three effective products; the full analytic radical expression is omitted because of its length.

Counts effective product variables using PjQ1 and P1Qk. Other products are expressed rationally through these, dividing by P1Q1. This yields NP(r) + NQ(−r) − 1 effective variables per charge sector rather than NP(r)NQ(−r).

Eliminate a nondynamical top form while retaining its flux integration constant. In this application the output is a family of quadratic axion branches, not an assertion that unconstrained minima of different branches have different energies.

Choose a census worldline, classify events in successive past light cones, and take N_i(t)/N(t) as t tends to infinity. The paper compares observer environments but does not establish convergence, uniqueness or a universal selection rule.

Track one state's evolving energy against the cooling horizon temperature, insert both into the heuristic emission rate, and test the late-time integral. The resulting divergence diagnoses persistent emission within the approximation, rather than a probability larger than one.

Count species at the same cutoff being solved for, substitute into the gravitational species prescription, and solve self-consistently. Retain an inequality when the tower provides only a lower bound on the full species count.
Sets the exterior horizon function to zero at the shell, evaluates the delivered energy at the resulting engulfment radius, and then minimizes over shell mass subject to a Compton-localization bound.

Uses spherical symmetry and Birkhoff's theorem to specify interior and exterior metrics. The shell equation of motion is evaluated in the adiabatic limit to obtain its asymptotic energy, including redshifted rest energy and gravitational self-energy.

Canonical normalization of the Kähler metric, a matrix-valued decay constant, and rotations into heavy/light axion directions separate kinetic parameters from instanton charges. Integrating out the heavy axion illustrates the effective potential; the authors state that their cosmological analysis retains both axion dynamics.

Moduli stabilization combines the α'^3 correction to the Kähler potential with a small-cycle nonperturbative superpotential, followed by generalized KK and winding loop corrections. Extended no-scale structure organizes the latter contribution to the scalar potential.

Complexified equations are solved with initial scalar phase θ tuned for late-time classicality after Wick rotation τ = τ₀ + it. The review reports numerical investigations alongside approximate analytic solutions.

The no-boundary Euclidean path integral sums regular compact geometries with one final boundary. Steepest descent replaces it by on-shell saddle contributions; an individual instanton receives approximate weight P ≃ exp(−2 Re S_E).

Higgs-related families are tested with BPS-string unitarity: current-algebra contributions k dim(G)/(k+h∨) must fit within the left-moving central charge. Highest-weight integrability and conformal-weight conditions are then applied to proposed worldsheet operators representing bulk matter.

The analysis combines anomaly equations, Lorentzian lattice embeddings, null-vector relations, and positivity of gauge kinetic terms. These restrict allowed tensor counts, numbers of gauge factors, and candidate infinite nonabelian families.
Classical groundwork uses KL/Bregman divergences, their Hessian Fisher metric, Legendre-dual coordinates, and covariance/Cramér–Rao interpretations.
Tower asymptotics use Schwinger parameters, Poisson resummation, and the leading dual-lattice zero mode. Sigma-model calculations use the covariant background-field method.

Quantum computations use the excited-state spectral representation, connected two-point functions integrated across opposite Euclidean-time half-spaces, and Euclidean vacuum overlaps with background parameters changing across τ = 0.

Compare discrete theories through a statistical divergence on shared observables. The source suggests flux vacua and asks whether an interpolating instanton action computes an appropriate path-integral comparison.

Interpolate between nearby vacua, expand with the covariant background-field method, include measure auxiliaries, and take the mixed endpoint Hessian. The imported expansion and the paper's information-interface application are distinct operations.

Choose either connected-correlator integration or a spectral sum. Regulate composite operators and infrared modes explicitly; apply Wick contraction only in free theories. The scalar, fermionic, and conformal examples use different deformation operators.

Schwinger-parametrize, differentiate to generate mass numerators, Poisson-resum, retain the continuum mode, and regulate the remaining integrals. This computes asymptotic scaling only when the dense-label and ultraviolet assumptions hold.

Use protected B-model data, exceptional collections, Ext groups and Riemann–Roch Euler pairings to determine chirality. Construct fractional-brane bound states through bifundamental VEVs, analyse gauge breaking and distinguish three chiral families from vector-like matter.

Analyse the four-dimensional N=1 F- and D-term potential using an inverse-volume expansion, the α′³ Kähler correction and W=W0+A3 exp(−a3T3)+A4 exp(−a4T4). Instanton coefficients are a3=a4=2π for the SO(8) configuration and 4π for rank-two instantons.

Search coordinate-divisor topologies and impose ksss ksij=kssi kssj for every i,j, making the divisor volume a square of one linear combination of two-cycle volumes. The hypersurface scans restrict to favourable geometries; complete intersections provide the explicit alternatives.

Invert nonsingular Rn × Rn submatrices of mn to construct the kernel. Schur-complement determinants convert the self-copy identity into a matrix-rank condition; left and right null vectors encode generalized KKBCJ constraints.

Solve a polynomial momentum expansion around BAS, fixing pole terms by lower-point factorization and adding local contact terms. Four-dimensional gauge-theory examples use spinor-helicity ansätze constrained by generalized KKBCJ relations.
At four points, assuming nonzero f2, rank one reduces to f6=f1, f1(s,t)=f2(s,t)f2(u,s)/f2(t,s), and f2(s,t)f2(u,s)f2(t,u)=f2(t,s)f2(u,t)f2(s,u). Locality supplies additional restrictions.

Numerically solve Ä + 3H Ȧ + ∂V/∂A = 0 with the axion included in the expansion rate. Scans over (V0, FA) yield today's equation of state and beta/cgamma, summarized by an FA-dependent numerical factor xi in Eq. (10).

Symmetries and superpotential holomorphy constrain instanton-induced effective Kähler and superpotential terms. Fermion zero modes are closed using higher-dimensional operators and mass insertions; the authors identify the effective Kähler contribution as dominant and Planck-size instantons as controlling the estimate.

Use the two-loop hypercharge beta function to incorporate the effect of the weak coupling and obtain cgamma,max. A Bayesian analysis combines theoretical bounds with birefringence and equation-of-state constraints, then marginalizes over beta, cgamma and FA.

Review Euclidean ovoid instantons, ds^2 = dτ^2 + a(τ)^2 dΩ3^2, with a vanishing linearly at both ends. Subtract the two background de Sitter actions to obtain forward and reverse probabilities; analytically continue at the poles to obtain open FRW evolutions.

Analyze radial null propagation through conformal time integral dt/a(t). The initial endpoint has vanishing physical diamond size; near the crunch, kinetic domination gives a(t) proportional to (ts − t)^(1/3), making the remaining conformal time finite.

Construct a schematic time-dependent Hamiltonian H(t) = ca(t)Ta on a finite-dimensional space. Initially slow variation permits adiabatic behavior; later Planck-time variation generating the full unitary algebra models chaos. Weak coupling to a smaller de Sitter system is tuned to reproduce a transition probability.

In the DFSZ construction, remove the three Goldstone modes eaten by W± and Z, identify the remaining axion direction, and project its couplings onto SM quark axial currents. Higgs-portal effects are estimated by inserting singlet VEVs into the scalar potential.

Project the fermion-coupled phase P1 onto the normalized Goldstone direction, then use the fermion Dirac equation to express its interaction through an axial-current derivative. The small P1 overlap produces a large effective axion decay constant.

Minimize the scalar potential using ∂V/∂vi = 0 and analyze the pseudoscalar mass matrix. Breaking one global U(1) leaves one massless Goldstone direction and n − 1 massive pseudoscalars; the general massive eigenstates are deliberately not displayed.

Use circle reduction and M-/F-theory fibre-base duality: the proposed gauged 2-form symmetry becomes a gauged 1-form symmetry in 5D. A second F-theory description relates it to the global gauge-group quotient induced by Mordell–Weil torsion.

Compute torsion and its embedding into individual SCFT defect groups from integral toric divisor relations. Integral intersections of wrapped curves with these relations constrain BPS-string charges; continued fractions determine resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities.

Use dual lattices, discriminant groups and discriminant pairings to describe screened surface-defect charges. Smith normal form gives an equivalent presentation of the finite discriminant group for a nondegenerate intersection matrix.

Obtain intrinsic/extrinsic forced conservation equations and approximate stress tensors and currents using homogeneous flat-space brane seeds. Matched asymptotic expansion relates these equations to constraints on a backreacted geometry.

Linearise KPV embedding and intrinsic variables, expand in temporal Fourier modes and spherical harmonics, and study non-radial and radial sectors separately. Radial harmonic mixing is expressed using Wigner 3j-symbols.
Construct stationary effective potentials at fixed boost rapidity, entropy, or temperature. A Legendre transformation gives the fixed-entropy action; extrema reproduce static blackfold equilibria.

Quantized conformal matter is represented semiclassically by a Polyakov–Liouville anomaly term. Evaporation is studied through both a sequence of static exterior states and light-cone evolution of the dilaton boundary.

Imported Euclidean-instanton CFT entropy formulas are applied to positive- and negative-mass configurations. Purity of the complete radiation/interior state permits computing radiation entropy by tracing either complementary subsystem.

Match a fixed physical smearing scale to the proper distance in the Taub-NUT metric, then demand that the source's coordinate support vanish. The resulting large integer-charge condition specifies the source's proposed regime of inflow control.

Specify a regulator, evaluate parity-odd two-point functions, and sum the KK tower. To retain the parent anomalous infinitesimal variation, include Pauli-Villars towers and a three-point function with a fluctuating Wilson-line insertion.

Sum parity-odd massive-fermion triangles with explicit charges, mass signs, multiplicities, and regulator. For Wilson-line chambers, include the changed zero-mode signs, opposite vector-multiplet chirality, and the cancellation of anomalous Wilson-line-dependent terms.

Construct X = ∂I2n+1^(0)/∂F, contract X with the integrated Wilson line, and vary the resulting local functional. This replaces a reduced anomalous variation by an explicit odd-dimensional counterterm.
One-loop KK contributions to Chern–Simons levels with ζ-function regularization, bulk anomaly inflow onto string worldsheets, and divisor intersection and adjunction arguments.
Anomaly descent and Bardeen–Zumino polynomials; the reduced-anomaly proof uses invariant symmetric polynomials and integration by parts, with expressions understood modulo total derivatives.

Use the level-one expression as a sufficient screen, then verify attainable charge intersections and evaluate the exact inequality whenever the screen fails. Compare the residual-divisor requirement with Kodaira positivity only under the geometric dictionary.

Compute inflow, identify the interacting normal-bundle R symmetry, remove the specified free center-of-mass contribution, and read central charges and gauge levels. The operation is conditional on the R-symmetry identification and sector split.
Analyze asymptotic plateau and tail limits, match the primordial perturbation amplitude and inflationary observables, and characterize late-time thawing with the CPL expansion wφ=w0+(1−a/a0)wa.

Use Jordan-to-Einstein-frame conformal transformations and canonical field redefinitions. For α-attractors, ϕ/mP=√(6α)tanh[φ/(√(6α)mP)] maps the noncanonical field interval into an unbounded canonical field.
Laplacian eigenmodes estimate KK masses on twisted tori. The localized solution is lifted using ds11²=T^(2/3)ds10²+T^(−4/3)(dz+C1)², followed by an explicit curvature analysis.

The IIA equations and Bianchi identities are expanded to first order in n⁻ᵇ. The localization equations reduce to Poisson equations; linearity permits summing Green's functions for intersecting sources, with additional F2 corrections required by its Bianchi identity and equation of motion.
Formal double T-duality supplies the smeared starting point. Anisotropic flux scalings are chosen to keep orientifold charge fixed while varying the coupling, internal radii and AdS radius.

Numerically integrate the potential-modified background equations for p=3, n=6 in the Einstein branch (α,β)=(1/2,0), using V(φ)=(φ²−λ²)². The potential changes background solutions while leaving the displayed perturbation-coefficient formulas unchanged.

In 3+1 dimensions, rewrite the dilaton-coupled Gauss–Bonnet contribution as Horndeski functions and apply the imported quadratic perturbation formalism. Stability requires GT, FT, GS, FS>0; cgw²=FT/GT and cs²=FS/GS. Subluminality is an additional condition.

Impose φ=q log R, integrate the Friedmann equation, and reduce the dilaton equation to a generally fifth-degree polynomial in q. Admissible branches require real q and strictly positive P0(q)/P1(q), with analogous conditions in the dual frame.

Impose cobordism triviality and anomaly cancellation jointly, then restrict gauge-group ranks, eliminate forbidden group choices and obtain dimension–rank relations. The review reports these output types while leaving the relevant theory class and calculation to cited works.

Start from large-N QCD vacuum results, continue them heuristically to N=3 at fixed Yukawa couplings, and apply the requirement of avoiding metastable de Sitter vacua. The output is a suggested necessary bound on v, without a supplied error estimate.

Combine topology with an independently specified anomaly calculation: trivialize the compactification cobordism class using defects, count their modes, and impose lower-dimensional anomaly cancellation. The torsion group alone is insufficient.

Place a conserved label into an evaporating black hole and ask whether the remaining entropy or spectrum can accommodate it. This is a consistency diagnostic whose conclusion depends on the assumed evaporation and remnant behavior.

Use charged-black-hole discharge or a long-range force comparison to motivate a sufficiently large charge-to-mass ratio. The two arguments are heuristic and require matching field content and normalization.

Reduce a specified spectrum, compute its vacuum-energy function, locate lower-dimensional vacua and test them against a separately stated consistency conjecture. The output is conditional on geometry, spin structure, loop control and treatment of additional fields.

Dualize the axion, apply the correctly normalized higher-form WGC, and convert string tension to an excitation scale. The photon application then substitutes f=m_γ/e; charge and spectrum assumptions remain necessary.
Construct a charged membrane bubble, match the interior and exterior fluxes, and test wall expansion. The reviewed sufficient condition uses a strictly superextremal wall in a flux-only AdS vacuum.

Use the nilpotent-orbit period expansion, suppress exponentially small corrections, and calculate central-charge phases, marginal-stability walls, and attractor extrema ∂i|Z|=0. Algebraic positivity conditions test whether split flows end at controlled attractors.

Relate zeros of constituent central charges along marginal-stability loci to forbidden interior singularities. Compare this obstruction with attractor positivity and the wall-crossing support condition Q(q)≥0, with Q negative on ker Z.

Analyze quadratic spectra and Hamiltonians to identify stable heavy propagation modes. For the extended timelike EFT, use a canonical transformation and resum spatial derivatives; the argument chiefly uses two-point dynamics rather than four-point scattering.

Solve classical heavy-field equations recursively in a derivative expansion, substitute their locally unique solutions into the action, and use a bookkeeping parameter on heavy-field derivatives. First derivatives of the light field remain nonperturbative.

Bayesian inference uses a product Gaussian likelihood for 123 redshift bins with constant per-bin uncertainty 0.05 K. MCMC evaluates signals through multidimensional linear interpolation of precomputed model grids.

Coupled gas-temperature and electron-fraction evolution includes adiabatic cooling, Compton, Lyα, Hawking-radiation and X-ray heating, plus ionization. Spin temperature follows radiative, collisional and Lyα couplings.

BlackHawk supplies Hawking spectra. Photon and electron/positron energy integrals, weighted by imported deposition-efficiency tables for dark-matter decay, determine hydrogen-ionization and heating inputs.

Use dimensional reduction and dilaton-radion Hessians, integrated higher-dimensional Einstein/dilaton equations, and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds. Analyze flux decay through Euclidean thin-wall instantons and compare their actions with brane instanton actions.

Linearize field equations, separate tensor/vector/scalar sectors, use spherical harmonics and physical AdS masses for BF comparisons. For static warped intervals, recast mode equations as Schrödinger problems with a factorized nonnegative operator under stated boundary conditions.

For the massless example, the spectator equation is integrated analytically using e-fold time. Linear density and pressure perturbations are evaluated in spatially flat gauge to estimate the regular relative entropy.
Numerical examples evolve the entropy-variable power spectra for m₂/m₁={0,10^−5,10^−3}, considering modes exiting the horizon 60 e-foldings before inflation ends.

Covariant Mukhanov–Sasaki equations are expanded in the original field basis and in a time-dependent kinematic vielbein basis. The comparison retains connection terms, mass matrices and friction rather than using the potential Hessian alone.

Evolve the sourced ALP Boltzmann equation with FRW expansion and radiation injection, then redshift using entropy conservation. The analytic matter-dominated approximation receives a reported normalization correction αc = 1.09 from numerical cosmological evolution.
Approximate scalar greybody factors by an energy-squared form, calibrating its integrated number flux to BlackHawk with κa ≃ 27.6. Use the nearly constant SM evaporation coefficient fev = 4.26×10^-3.

Propagate photon–ALP mixing through redshifting magnetic domains with photoelectric and Compton absorption, using an imported perturbative recursion. Massive ALPs are treated with coupled decay/absorption Boltzmann equations discretized in redshift.

Gravitational fixed-point locations are taken from existing beta functions in background and fluctuation approximations. In the latter, effective universality is assumed to identify the Newton-coupling avatars with the three-graviton avatar.

Functional renormalization group for the effective average action, using the Wetterich flow equation, a diagonal Litim regulator, a P⁻¹F vertex expansion and momentum projections onto the retained operators.

The calculation uses a flat Euclidean background, metric fluctuations and York decomposition, with gauge parameters α→0 and β→0. Anomalous dimensions from regulator insertions are omitted in the perturbative approximation used throughout; their leading contributions remain in canonical scaling terms.

For the anomaly argument, the authors decompose cocharacters by simple factors and relate their norms to center quadratic forms. Narain cocharacters have even integral norm and dual-Mikhailov cocharacters integral norm; explicit Sp coweights supply the non-simply-laced contribution. The imported criterion is Σi mi αi ki²=0 modulo integers.

Decompose the real momentum space orthogonally into the non-Abelian root plane E and its complement F. Compute lattice projections and intersections, express cocharacters in coweight bases, and identify their classes in the center modulo coroots.

Extract radial frequencies from central-density power spectra. Reconstruct scalar strain from the Jordan-frame Newman–Penrose scalar or hs ≃ 2α0(φ−φ∞), then integrate against detector noise spectra for SNR. Detector estimates assume optimal scalar orientation F0 = 1/2.

Use an Einstein-frame spherical Z3 evolution system with 1+log slicing, HRSC finite differences, adaptive dissipation, and third-order SSP Runge–Kutta time integration at Courant factor 0.25. The authors report resolution convergence and outer-boundary robustness.

Construct initial stars by integrating modified TOV equations outward and shooting to Schwarzschild–de Sitter asymptotics. Transform static areal coordinates to maximal isotropic coordinates for evolution.

Apply holographic renormalization with a radial cutoff, Gibbons–Hawking–York and local counterterms, plus the Gauss–Bonnet boundary completion. Express the completed Gauss–Bonnet term through the Euler characteristic and reduce that characteristic to fixed-point contributions.

Use Killing-spinor bilinears to construct a local orthonormal frame and metric/gauge-field form, then combine bilinear identities, the Bianchi identity, and Killing-spinor integrability to establish the two-derivative equations.
Rewrite the four-derivative Euler–Lagrange equations in terms of two-derivative equation tensors and their derivatives, making the embedding of two-derivative solutions explicit.

Start from the imported Lorentzian ansatz ε1(N) = 2ξΓ/[π(4N² + Γ²)]. Integrate ε1 = −H′/H to obtain H(N), generate the hierarchy through εn+1 = d ln|εn|/dN, and use the Friedmann equations and a field–e-fold relation to reconstruct a potential.

Calculate potential parameters ε = (V′/V)²/2, η = V″/V and ζ² = V′V‴/V²; take inflation to end at ε = 1 or η = 1. Use an approximate field integral for N and the formulas ns = 1 − 6ε + 2η and r = 16ε, then compare predictions with published observational contours.

Recast parametric crossing-symmetric dispersion relations into Robertson representations with positive measures. Apply imported Bieberbach–Rogosinski coefficient inequalities to normalized amplitudes; for real poles, use Schiffer–Bargmann decomposition and Goodman bounds.

Use Markov brothers' polynomial inequalities for finite coefficient bounds. Derive Toeplitz determinant conditions through the Carathéodory/Herglotz correspondence and trigonometric moment problem, then expand these conditions near a=0.

Use partial-wave inversion and positivity of Gegenbauer polynomials or their derivatives to construct positive linear combinations of Wilson coefficients. Locality requires W(n−m,m)=0 for n<m; the main GFT implementation starts with a local expansion rather than explicitly solving those constraints.

Map the local R + R² theory with cosmological constant to a scalar potential through the standard F(R) construction. Numerically impose the conjectural potential bounds throughout the prescribed field interval while varying the constants c and f.

Use imported one-loop beta functions: the marginal-coupling flow is analytically solvable and decoupled from the Einstein–Hilbert sector, whose equations are integrated numerically. Sample UV deformations and extract IR combinations at a sufficiently large RG time, approximately t = 30.

Remove the arbitrary reference scale by expressing couplings in IR Planck units, using the asymptotic behavior of the dimensionless Newton coupling. Identify the squared RG scale with the covariant Laplacian/d’Alembertian to reconstruct local coefficients and logarithmic non-local form factors.

Compute component scalings, add contraction and derivative contributions, then group operators by coupling and Planck order. The paper applies this imported bookkeeping to detect time-neutral families that would undermine a Wilsonian truncation.

Use an isometric reduction circle to identify the lower-dimensional dilaton, reduce the remaining metric, then T-dualize the second circle. In this paper the resulting coupling is used as a grading parameter for time-dependent quantum corrections.

Compute optical depth by integrating cross section against the environmental four-current, then use P=exp(−T) for interaction-free propagation. Include redshifting energies, a thermal CMB distribution, and a piecewise free-electron history for Thomson scattering.

Integrate occupation numbers over a homogeneous comoving density of states, restricting the inflationary contribution to modes that became superhorizon. Combine this density with ALP-photon fermion-production cross sections or ALP decay widths and subsequent photon-photon scattering.

Rescale the scalar field to ϕ=aφ, solve Fourier-mode equations and use Bogolyubov coefficients or squeezing parameters to estimate occupation numbers. A small-mass expansion of Hankel-function solutions estimates corrections during inflation.

Split the path into constant-vacuum regions and a narrow transition region; package the latter into a metric-dependent tension T. Take δs→0 and, where possible, extremize the exponent with respect to the remaining metric variable. Alternative field-space-distance parameterizations are also presented.
Use Ψ=exp(iS/ℏ), expand S=S₀+ℏS₁+…, and retain S₀. The leading WDW equation is Hamilton–Jacobi-like; parameterized field-space curves and a function C(s) express the action as an integral of f/C.

For time-only fields, the proposed general solution expresses C² and field velocities using derivatives of f. Ratios of velocities give differential relations among minisuperspace coordinates, subsequently used to integrate constant-vacuum action segments.
Replica twist correlators are uniformized to a 2n-point function in the original CFT. An OPE expansion permits termwise analytic continuation of the replica index to n=1.

Large-c factorization organizes the leading correlator as Wick contractions, expressible through a Haffnian. Corrections include stress-tensor exchange, dimension shifts and double-trace OPE-coefficient shifts; the latter use imported Virasoro-bootstrap data and a Barnes double-Gamma expansion.

The bulk procedure requantizes the scalar on the first-order backreacted metric and solves semiclassical Einstein equations again. Regularity, boundary normalizability and unit Klein-Gordon norm fix wavefunction data. Metric and shape contributions to area are evaluated perturbatively, using AdS-Rindler coordinates for displacement.
Use a relativistic two-state Hamiltonian with V_a=V_W+δV_a and δV_a=[(g′A′)²−2g′p·A′]/(2p). Resonance requires 2pV_a+m²_aa=m²_ss≈m²_s, hence a sufficiently positive active matter contribution.

Approximate production by Γ_s=Γ_a〈P_{a→s}〉, averaging oscillations over exponentially distributed elastic-scattering times. Solve dR/dt=Γ_s(1−R), linearize for small R, integrate the direction angle analytically, and evaluate the remaining temperature–momentum integral numerically.

The numerical yield uses tabulated active-neutrino damping rates rather than only Γ_a≈C_a²T⁴p, and a more general electroweak matter potential than its low-temperature limit. Present-day oscillations are explored with numerical Schrödinger evolution and second-order time-dependent perturbation theory.

Identify all independent scales, specify fixed couplings and discrete labels, nondimensionalize and compare dimensions. Apply the same common-scale cancellation to state-counting thresholds. In this paper the method concerns proposed quantum-break times and the emergence-motivated species count.

Vary before gauge fixing, solve the metric and scalar background equations jointly, fix the nonzero conformal compensator and match the reduced action. In this application the outputs are AdS/dS branches and the parameter dictionary to topologically massive gravity.

Extract derivative axial-current couplings of the top and new quark and infer the axion–gluon interaction. Use VEV hierarchies and the bottom-Yukawa perturbativity requirement to estimate enhancement factors and attainable symmetry-breaking scales.

Specify the charge assignments, full renormalizable scalar potential and allowed Yukawa interactions. Expand all scalar fields around their VEVs and identify gauge-eaten directions, the remaining axion, and massive neutral and charged scalar combinations.

Search the secondary fan by following a path in divisor-volume space across triangulations, then iteratively incorporate corrected Kähler coordinates. Compute genus-zero Gopakumar–Vafa invariants through mirror symmetry and use high-degree growth along sampled rays to estimate instanton convergence.

Solve integer flux constraints using p^a=(κ̃_{abc}M^c)^{-1}K_b, with 0≤−M·K/2≤χ_f/4, p inside the mirror Kähler cone, and K·p=0. These give a perturbatively flat valley z=pτ with vanishing perturbative superpotential; mirror instantons then generate a racetrack.

Count orientifold ED3 fermion zero modes and construct F-theory uplifts. Smooth rigid divisors provide superpotential contributions; imposing h^{2,1}(D̂)=0 makes the intermediate Jacobian trivial and the corresponding Pfaffian a constant.

Choose integer fluxes so the perturbative part of the mirror type IIA prepotential contributes exactly zero along a perturbatively flat valley. The remaining leading instantons have GV invariants −2 and 252 and racetrack exponents 7/29 and 7/28, producing an exponentially small flux superpotential.

Identify rigid prime toric divisors whose F-theory uplifts have trivial intermediate Jacobian to obtain nonvanishing ED3 or gaugino-condensation terms with constant prefactors. Assess worldsheet corrections through the sizes of successive instanton terms along a sample of 1,728 rays.

Analyze solutions depending on one spacetime coordinate; integrate their Einstein-frame line elements and scalar kinetic metrics to compare proper spacetime and field-space distances. In the CY3 case, use harmonic functions Hi=ai y+ci and continuous matching across flux jumps.

Reduce axion-winding configurations on S1, retaining the radion backreaction, then match the resulting 3d profiles to 4d strings. Extract near-wall asymptotics of distance integrals and curvature; incomplete gamma functions enter the circle and USp(32) analyses.

Matches KK masses against completely wrapped brane masses in a common lower-dimensional Einstein frame. For the twelve-dimensional example, decomposes field representations under SL(3)→SL(2), counts degrees of freedom, and imposes truncations and a section condition.

Uses the toroidal KK quadratic form l_i G^(ij) l_j, metric determinants, quotient volumes V(T^D)/|Γ|, and the equal-momentum tower. A special angle θ_D is selected by equating that tower's squared mass to V(O^D)^(−2/D).

Flavor and EDM estimates use mass insertions. The authors report checks against SUSY FLAVOR v2.5 and use that code for muon g−2 parameter regions, incorporating the cited LHC slepton searches. These are reported numerical checks, not independently repeated here.

Random O(1) matrix coefficients are selected to fit fermion masses, mixings and CP phases, including canonical normalization of kinetic terms. For 1000 accepted trials, absolute real and imaginary components of soft matrices are averaged separately and normalized by the average absolute eigenvalue.

Calculations use model-specific CLASS versions and MontePython v3.3. Best-fit searches employ repeated short, modified Metropolis–Hastings chains with decreasing steps and enhanced likelihood sensitivity, because numerical-gradient minimization could become trapped in local minima.

Sequential MCMC tests use Planck 2018 TTTEEE+lensing and BAO, then add Pantheon to define the baseline. Finalists are tested with Planck replaced by WMAP+ACT or with CMB data replaced by background probes; a final extension adds RSD, cosmic chronometers and Lyα BAO.

Three criteria distinguish posterior compatibility, joint-fit compatibility and model preference: Gaussian tension from mean differences and quadrature errors; QDMAP using best-fit χ² with and without SH0ES; and ΔAIC penalizing added complexity. The reported acceptance cut is approximately ΔAIC≤−6.91 relative to ΛCDM. χ² denotes −2 ln L.

Expands BFSS fields in Matsubara modes. Rescaled zero modes yield the Euclidean IKKT action at leading high temperature; integrating nonzero modes supplies corrections expressed through IKKT expectation values χ_i.
Approximates mixed IKKT correlators by products: χ₅≈N²χ₂χ₁ and χ₆≈N²χ₂χ₁/d. Uses the imported expression χ₂=(d−1)(1−1/N²) when restoring the final spectrum amplitude.

Computes E=−∂βlnZ and C_V=(∂E/∂T)_V. Thermal energy-density variance is T²C_V/R⁶, and energy-momentum correlations source scalar and tensor metric fluctuations through linear Einstein perturbation equations at Hubble exit.

Use normalized Jacobi-theta-function solutions of the magnetized Dirac equation and their products on T⁶. Supersymmetry supplies the corresponding bosonic profiles. Matter fields are rescaled so the superpotential is holomorphic and their Kähler metrics are real functions of moduli.

For the selected F-term quartic interaction, insert a complete Landau-level eigenfunction basis into a four-profile overlap. The authors use massive/zero-mode orthogonality to express it through products of three-profile Yukawa overlaps and compare the result with the supergravity potential.

Expand the symmetrized-trace DBI determinant through O(F⁴), decompose F into background and fluctuations, and integrate the gauge, scalar kinetic and selected quartic coefficients over the torus. Non-Abelian ordering is handled by averaging traces over permutations.

Adopts an imported entropy prescription: define total entropy from nonadiabatic pressure, subtract the sum of intrinsic component entropies, and study the resulting gauge-invariant relative entropy S_rel rather than relying on the tangent/normal perturbation decomposition.

Derives component energy and pressure perturbations at linear order in spatially flat gauge, evaluates them on the slow-roll attractor, and supplements the analytic zero-axion-potential limit with numerical evolution including nonzero axionic potentials.
Use normalized positive measures and convex-hull geometry for analytic bounds, and SDPB optimization of positive functionals for numerical bounds involving several coefficient ratios.

Expand the dispersion relation in s(s+u) and u. Crossing produces redundant sum rules, first at eight derivatives; eliminating EFT coefficients gives f-type and g-type null constraints on UV spectral densities. Higher-order sum rules supply additional constraints.

Match low-energy amplitudes to Wigner-d partial waves through doubly-subtracted fixed-u dispersion relations. Spectral densities are ρiJ=Im AiJ; the positive combinations include ρ2J±ρ1J for even J and ρ3J for J≥2, with ρ4J=(-1)^Jρ3J.

Gauge nonanomalous one-form symmetry subgroups using sums over H²(M,L). Coprime finite first homology removes nontrivial backgrounds. Prime-power factorization of Abelian TQFTs and the Chinese remainder theorem isolate factors in the extended higher-charge test.

Shrink a topological boundary tube to an algebra anyon, interpret multiplicities through punctured-disk Hilbert spaces, and use junction deformations to obtain algebra axioms. A mesh dual to a triangulation gives the geometric condensation construction.

Compute partition functions by surgery and Gauss sums. K-matrix quadratic refinements define auxiliary Abelian TQFTs; symplectic Gaussian reciprocity relates the Chern–Simons matrix and surgery linking matrix under coprimality conditions.

Estimate perturbative decay widths, reheating temperature, branching fractions, entropy dilution, dark-radiation contributions and nonthermal axino yields. The reheating estimate assumes instantaneous conversion of modulus energy into radiation.

Expand Kähler interactions into component D-terms, use equations of motion to identify mass suppression, and transform to the canonical mass basis. For symmetry-breaking matter, kinetic mixing and cubic interactions from the matter kinetic term must be treated together.

After imported perturbative gravitational anomaly cancellation, the authors use bordism classification of invertible topological theories and evaluate the anomaly on representative generators, including lens spaces, products with HP² and non-Spin manifolds.

Identify the full background structure, compute its bordism generators, and evaluate the anomaly phase on each representative. The type IIB application combines fermionic η-invariants with a self-dual-field anomaly theory.

Explicit tools include APS index theorems, Dirac and Rarita-Schwinger η-invariants, signature η-invariants, torsion pairings and quadratic-refinement Arf invariants. Adams and Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequences underpin the reported bordism computation; its details are deferred.

Modify the self-dual-field Chern–Simons quadratic refinement by a duality-bundle torsion term, then evaluate the anomaly shift on bordism generators. The reported cancellation is spectrum-dependent and remains conditional on one non-Spin Arf sign.

Promote Grassmannian constructions of polarized K3 surfaces to Grassmann bundles over P1; impose trivial canonical bundle by adjunction and compute intersections and characteristic classes using Chow rings, top Chern classes and Schubert calculus. Intersection calculations used Schubert2 in Macaulay2.

Identify mirror maps with modular functions or Hauptmoduln. For alternative quartic-K3 fibrations, compute Picard–Fuchs systems and take the large-base degeneration to the fiber operator, supporting independence from the fibration twist.

At large base volume, use the hyperbolic upper-half-plane metric and modular identifications to integrate lengths along geodesic semicircles joining special points. This replaces slowly converging local period expansions with exact asymptotic distance expressions.

Calculate potential slow-roll parameters ε=(V′/V)²/2, η=V″/V and ζ²=V′V‴/V², integrate N=∫dϕ/√(2ε), and use n_s=1−6ε+2η, α_s=16εη−24ε²−2ζ² and r=16ε. Compare the resulting trajectories with published joint n_s–r contours.

Use F=df/dR, the conformal relation ĝμν=Fgμν, and V=(RF−f)/(2F²) to connect Jordan and Einstein frames. Express the constant-roll condition as an equation for Ĥ(ϕ), solve its nonconstant branch, reconstruct R(ϕ), and substitute it into each model's f_R.

Substitute the logarithmic model and constant-roll condition into the metric background equations, approximate the resulting equation, and solve a differential equation for H(t). Reconstruct a scalar potential and differentiate it for swampland tests.

Use four inflationary indicators εi, with ε2=0, to calculate ns and r; the quoted tensor ratio is r=48ε3²/(1+ε3)². Explore dependence on n and β through parameter plots rather than a stated statistical fitting procedure.

Interpret a flux-threaded wormhole as two ends carrying mutually dual charges; bring the ends together to form a soliton. Universal grading and irreducibility of graded components over the adjoint subcategory organize the general categorical argument.

Quantize a nontrivial-cycle holonomy as a wavefunction in L²(G), with gauge transformations acting by conjugation. Use its kernel Z, compact-group representation theory and Peter–Weyl decomposition to identify generated charges.

Explain Wilson-line endability using operators at conical singularities. A soliton's spatial topology, compactified to M, defines a cone insertion and a charged defect Hilbert space on M, extending the smooth-point local-operator construction.

Integral divisor–curve duality is obtained using Poincaré duality. The zero-section/generic-fiber pair and pullbacks from the base are projected out; unimodularity of the base intersection form preserves a dual pairing for the remaining gauge divisors and charged curves.

Anomaly cancellation determines matter multiplicities. Their vanishing, together with divisor-effectivity arguments and sometimes Zariski decomposition, forces Weierstrass coefficients to vanish and produces explicit Mordell–Weil torsion forms. Elliptic-curve addition also identifies primitive sections in the abelian example.

Evolve visible and dark energy densities separately from reheating to neutrino decoupling using entropy conservation or specified entropy injection. Express their final ratio through inflaton branching ratios and sector-dependent energy and entropy g-factors.

Use imported open-string entropy formulas, compare microcanonical entropies with a black 3-brane, differentiate entropy to obtain temperature, and infer effective energy and entropy degrees of freedom near the Hagedorn temperature.

Canonically normalize gauge vectors using the negative-definite kinetic matrix, diagonalize the Hermitian gravitino charge matrix, and compare charge-squared contributions to the scalar potential with the magnetic WGC cutoff.

Construct explicit electric-frame gaugings from special-Kähler sections and quaternionic-Kähler Killing vectors and moment maps; evaluate critical points, gravitino masses and canonically normalized scalar spectra.

Classify matter fermion interactions into seven structures with the gravitino set to zero for that analysis. Inspect derivatives of N or the FI composite function with respect to chiral-projection multiplets to identify maximal inverse powers of the supersymmetry-breaking auxiliary quantities.

Use operator-dimension power counting: coefficients of dimension-δ operators, δ>4, must be suppressed by Λcut^(4−δ). Free massless matter equations of motion simplify the leading singular terms; discarded terms carry additional matter-mass factors and need separate scale accounting.

Construct composite multiplets through superconformal multiplication and chiral projection, then apply the D-density formula to obtain bosonic, fermionic and gravitino terms. The liberated off-shell action is organized as derivatives of a composite real function N.

The scalar Banks–Zaks test computes one-loop differences between multi-meson dimensions. Fermionic mesons require identifying the lightest operator after mixing among several spin structures; that calculation is left for future work.

Tests compare anomalous dimensions using small-parameter perturbation theory, large-N and large-Nf expansions, and semiclassical large-charge results. Many input dimensions are imported calculations; the paper evaluates their implications for the proposed inequality.
Mellin–Barnes residues produce Lauricella F_C series. Their gamma-function structure supplies asymptotic boundary data and combinatorial constructions of differential operators.
Rotate the Gauss–Manin system by its ε=0 homogeneous Wronskian, then integrate recursively in ε using known lower-sector inhomogeneities.
An alternative Bessel representation constructs equal-mass operators. Mirror symmetry and Γ-class evaluations determine D=2 asymptotics and transformations to integral-cycle period bases.

Uses curved-target-space slow-roll equations and modular expressions for the spectral index and tensor ratio. Numerical trajectories are integrated to the end of inflation to obtain N_*; analytic hyperbolic geodesics provide a comparison for projected trajectory shapes.

Uses the geometric volume measure √det(G) dφ¹dφ² on a modular fundamental domain. Its area is πμ²/3 = −2π/(3R_fs); the sufficient-inflation fraction is vol(B_F)/vol(F), avoiding a volume regularization within this quotient.

Scans lattices of initial field values using truncated Eisenstein series. Separate constraints on N_*, n_RR and r are imposed, followed by μ variations and examination of distributions in observable space.

Estimates the CEH collective-coordinate measure by dimensional reasoning: ρ⁻⁵dρ, normalization factors for bosonic zero modes, and one-loop running proportional to (ρΛ)^(3b/2). This is explicitly an educated guess rather than an explicit determinant calculation.

Relates the gauge configuration to EH curvature, evaluates topological action contributions, and adapts previously computed Dirac indices for SU(2) representations to identify fermion zero modes and induced chiral vertices.

Closes light-quark zero modes with mass insertions m_iρ and integrates over instanton size. The QCD potential coefficient is matched to chiral perturbation theory; the coupled two-axion cosine potential is then minimized and its mass matrix discussed.

Uses the extremal horizon equation and classical censorship mass function Θ(a/L,P), together with S = π(r_H²+a²)/(ℓ_G²|1−a²/L²|). Parent and emitted entropies are evaluated directly; survivor parameters can be determined numerically from conservation and extremality.

Discusses the emitted object's possible later evolution using an imported brane-action criterion for Seiberg–Witten instability, then argues qualitatively that its asymptotic origin may make it relevant to quantum-corrected black holes.

Bounds survivor entropy below by that of an extremal nonrotating black hole with the same charge. The final-minus-initial entropy is then bounded by (L²/ℓ_G²)Ψ(A,P), whose asserted positivity is examined through limits and monotonicity.

Construct form-factor discontinuities above charged-pair threshold using Cutkosky cuts of tree amplitudes, massive spinor-helicity variables and an auxiliary photon-to-spectator amplitude. Recover form factors by dispersion relations, subtracting F1 according to its zero-transfer normalization.

Fourier-transform the eikonal amplitude into impact-parameter space, diagonalize its helicity matrix, and express the phase through graviton-pole residues and discontinuities weighted by Bessel functions. Vector Sudakov double logarithms are treated by RG resummation and numerical integration.
Expand helicity amplitudes in angular-momentum partial waves with Wigner rotation matrix elements. Combine the optical theorem with J≥|h_s| and bounds on angular-momentum matrix elements.

Remove unphysical kinematic singularities using a spin/helicity-dependent regulated amplitude. Apply fixed-t Cauchy dispersion relations to its even s derivatives, subtracting EFT poles and cuts through scale μ.

Use Monge gauge Xμ=ξμ and expand the brane action about a static plane. Rescaling transverse fluctuations produces canonical scalar kinetic terms plus the tension contribution; the DBI expansion additionally yields Maxwell electrodynamics.

Review scalar rolling and late-time scaling solutions. For cosmological compactifications, reconstruct higher-dimensional stress-energy from Einstein equations using external and internal scale exponents, then impose energy-condition inequalities.

Chow-ring pushforwards evaluate quadruple divisor intersections of hypersurfaces in blown-up P² bundles. Results reduce to base triple intersections involving characteristic classes K, gauge divisors Σs, and the section-intersection class W01.

Match geometric fluxes to one-loop-exact 3D Chern–Simons couplings using ΘĪĴ=−Θ³ᴰĪĴ, then solve for chiral indices without explicitly constructing matter surfaces. Auxiliary CY threefold triple intersections determine phase-dependent sign and floor functions through 5D Chern–Simons matching.

Encode integrated fluxes as Θ=Mφ. Quotient homologically trivial surfaces and impose symmetry constraints in either order. When the required inverse or pseudoinverse exists, the constrained pairing is MC=M″−Qᵀ(M′)⁺Q; its integral domain must also be retained.

Use the attractor mechanism and fake-superpotential gradient flows for static, spherically symmetric black holes. A nonnegative sum-of-squares rewriting bounds the ADM mass, assuming suitable horizon behavior, and identifies extremal flow solutions.

Introduce dual coordinates Ỹ_I=F_I/F and Legendre-transform arguments to study convexity and straighten BPS flows. Compute genus-zero Gopakumar–Vafa invariants through mirror symmetry, GKZ/Picard–Fuchs equations, periods, mirror maps and Yukawa couplings.

Treat wrapped instantons and nonlocal counterterms through trans-series and nested internal integrals. The authors argue for finite local contributions after integration/resummation, conditional on suppression or decoupling of sufficiently high orders of nonlocality.

Organize flux equations into rank-zero, rank-seven and rank-eight tensors, including curvature polynomials, quantum corrections and membrane sources. Match coupling scalings using the authors' under-bracket and over-bracket scheme.

Count curvature, flux and derivative operators at fixed powers of the dual IIA coupling and eleven-dimensional Planck mass. Relative signs in the scaling constraints determine whether finitely or infinitely many operators contribute at a specified order.

Diagonalize masses in canonically normalized variables and examine transverse stability after uplift. For logarithmic Kähler geometry, transform to canonical inflaton variables or disk coordinates to obtain E-model and T-model plateau potentials.

At Step II use KII=KI+[FX²/(FX²+Vinfl)]X X̄. When KI is not in the required flat form, the authors use equivalent Kähler-transformed formulations; their compact prescription is WII=WI+(W0+FX X)exp[−κ(T)/2], with κ defined by the stated holomorphic restriction of KI.

Step II introduces a nilpotent multiplet X²=0, gravitino and supersymmetry-breaking parameters, and a chosen inflationary function. Canonical-field mass spectra are studied along the resulting valleys; extra potential terms freeze or merge light directions.

Step I uses quadratic generalized-flux superpotentials, solves W_flux=∂W_flux=0, checks tadpole/Bianchi constraints and computes moduli mass spectra. Restriction to the flat loci gives effective logarithmic Kähler potentials.

The preliminary parameter study fixes the physical matter density and comoving distance to last scattering to Planck-based ΛCDM values, assumes z*=1100, and determines Λs0 through the distance integral. Its illustrative curves neglect radiation; this construction is distinct from the subsequent full likelihood analysis.

Modified CosmoMC samples background and perturbation parameters using Planck 2018 temperature, polarization, and lensing, alone or combined with BAO including Ly-α DR14, Galaxy consensus, MGS, and 6dFGS. MCEvidence supplies Bayesian model comparisons. A restricted z†=2.32 model is also fitted.

For analytical background evolution, neglect radiation and glue negative-Λ and positive-Λ Friedmann–Lemaître scale-factor solutions at t†. Impose a(0)=0 and a(t0)=1; examine expansion, deceleration, and jerk.

Forecast with a Fisher matrix for zero-mean Gaussian E/B multipoles. Their covariance contains EE, EB, and BB spectra, instrumental noise, and foreground residuals where included. Fiducial rotations and EB are zero; the paper also compares fixing and marginalizing the recombination angle.
