Metric variation yields modified Friedmann equations involving F=f1′+2f2′LM. The authors integrate the selected continuity equation and insert their functions f1 and f2 to obtain the model H(z) used in observational fitting.

The authors combine the prescribed scale factor, coupled inflaton/radiation continuity equations and Friedmann equation to reconstruct φ(t), t(φ) and an inverse-power potential with field dependence V(φ) proportional to φ^[-4(1−f)/f]. This records their reconstruction without validating its normalization.

They express slow-roll and perturbation observables in terms of model parameters and e-folds, then use parameter-space plots to compare r and ns with Planck contours and impose distance, de Sitter and TCC criteria.

Use modified CosmoMC with CAMB and Metropolis–Hastings sampling. Four chains are run with a stated Gelman–Rubin convergence criterion R−1<0.01. These are reported numerical methods, not independently reproduced results.

Fit the primordial spectrum directly to Planck 2018 TT, EE, TE and low-multipole polarization likelihoods, collectively labeled Planck TT+Pol. The analysis varies two inflation-spectrum parameters alongside four standard cosmological parameters.

Apply slow-roll and quasi-stationary radiation approximations to obtain 3H(1+Q)φ̇≈−V,φ and 4ργ≈3Qφ̇². The authors use a Q evolution equation, its stated e-fold relation and an N(k) mapping to construct a model-dependent primordial spectrum.

A3C reinforcement learning changes one of eight flux entries by ±1, giving 16 actions. A four-hidden-layer dense policy network receives rewards balancing consistency and phenomenological requirements. Episodes allow up to 500 steps; the source reports training for 15,000,000 episodes.

The GA repeatedly selects flux vectors by fitness, performs crossover and applies mutation, with cloning and survival options. Its operator library contains eight selection, nine crossover and nine mutation operators; 29 hyperparameters are tuned using minibatch trials and correlations with final distance from the target.

Analyse both pooled and separate GA/RL samples with PCA and flux-correlation maps. The authors also report equivalent structure under t-SNE. Individual GA runs are inspected to expose run-dependent sampling variations rather than relying only on the aggregate sample.

Field displacement operators impose initial one-point functions. Equal-time canonical commutators and the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula reduce BRST physicality to bulk constraints and boundary terms; ghost mode expansions handle nonlocalized configurations.

Heisenberg equations separate classical one-point dynamics from quantum correlator contributions. Leading pair-production backreaction uses tree-level scalar mode functions, Minkowski-vacuum initial correlators, and renormalization of coincident correlators.

Impose θ̇ = ω = constant and ∂θV = 0, eliminate H and radial acceleration from the background equations, and obtain an ODE relating the potential to f. Fixing the negative curvature simplifies that ODE.

An adapted change of variables from the Noether symmetry method reduces the minisuperspace problem to elementary u,v,w equations. Constant angular velocity selects v = Cw cos(ωt), w = Cw sin(ωt); the Einstein equations additionally require the Hamiltonian constraint EL = 0.

Match a low-energy forward pole to a positive cross-section integral through contour deformation. The operation tests a necessary UV-completion condition and is applied here to distinguish pure Galileons from DBI-protected Galileons.

Enumerate admissible lowest-point amplitudes at fixed spectrum and derivative order, solve Ward and softness constraints, then apply constructible higher-point tests. Locality here is an input restriction on seeds; allowing cubic interactions requires exchange poles and changes the admissible ansatz.

Use the scalar seed as a superamplitude basis and differentiate with respect to external Grassmann variables. The operation supplies the Ward identities used for quartic locality and quintic parameter constraints; it does not itself ensure that all components are local.

Reconstruct higher-point amplitudes from factorization and prescribed softness, then vary the momentum-conserving deformation. Residual deformation dependence rules out the proposed assumptions. A passing test only supports a candidate at the multiplicities and coupling orders actually examined.

Use the Lorentz-invariant Callan–Symanzik regulator Rk = Zφk², dimensional regularisation, and a flowing counterterm action. The renormalised flow is ∂tΓk = ½ Tr(Gk∂tRk) − ∂tSct,k; the masslike regulator preserves the spectral representation without introducing extra propagator poles or cuts.

Apply a vertex expansion and TT projection, insert spectral representations for graviton and ghost propagators, and perform the remaining loop-momentum integrals analytically. Single-particle spectral peaks give closed analytic flows; integrating the spectral flow produces the continuum.

Eliminate the scalar field using the e-fold relation, then project a shared parameter family into the planes (r,V'/V) and (n_s,V'/V). This operation requires consistent formulas and a specified real branch for every coordinate.

Differentiate a specified potential, evaluate the brane slow-roll factors, integrate the field trajectory, and substitute the horizon-crossing field into the perturbation expressions. The printed normalization and integration sign must be retained until a consistent convention is established.

Expand, differentiate, integrate, solve for the field, and substitute into shared diagnostics. Test endpoint omission and high-energy control separately. This abstraction preserves the source’s input restrictions and exposes where inconsistent derivatives or signs invalidate the procedure.

Use the Bergshoeff–de Roo heterotic action through O(α′), including the Lorentz Chern–Simons contribution to H. An imported lemma removes implicit torsionful-connection variations that contribute only at higher order.

Compute correction sources from zeroth-order T-tensors, solve radial equations in ten dimensions, then reduce using α′-corrected field relations. Killing-spinor equations classify supersymmetric sign choices; asymptotic metric coefficients determine masses.

Entropy is evaluated with an imported gauge-invariant generalization of Wald's prescription. The extremal application extrapolates a formula originally derived for nonextremal bifurcate horizons to a spatial horizon section.

Resolve the singular D7 surface by blowing up its self-intersection locus, lift the flux curves, and compute charge through curve intersections and adjunction. The intersection of distinct irreducible image curves is nonnegative and therefore cannot weaken the charge lower bound.

Use Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing and the Atiyah–Singer index theorem to count D7 parameters. Bound stabilization constraints using a blow-up along the flux curve, exact sheaf/cohomology sequences, and the curve line-bundle bound h⁰≤degree+1.

Use a spectral-parameter Lax connection whose flatness reproduces the field equations, transform it by the period mapping h, and evaluate the action after imposing the A and Ā constraints. Charge orthogonality of the trace restricts action terms to opposite-charge pairings.

Write Q = hQrefh⁻¹ and B = h⁻¹dh, then decompose B into integer eigenspaces of ad Qref. Projecting the sigma-model equations onto these charge modes converts them into algebraic restrictions and differential equations. Flatness of B supplies the corresponding Bianchi identities.

Zeros of extremal functionals constrain saturating spectra; modular-form arguments establish uniqueness in special cases. Supplying additional low-lying bulk scalar dimensions strengthens numerical bounds when the bulk gap alone is insufficient.

Represent the annulus as a four-point function of defect-endpoint twist fields of dimension c/16. Positive expansions of bulk and boundary characters into one-dimensional conformal blocks allow analytic correlator functionals to be applied to annulus crossing.

Linear functionals act on reduced Virasoro characters; positivity excludes proposed g values and gaps. Numerical functionals use derivatives at t=exp(z), z=0, optimized by semidefinite programming with SDPB; increasing derivative order enlarges the search space.

Estimate thermal tunnelling through the O(3)-invariant Euclidean bounce and thick-wall approximation. Percolation uses Γ/H⁴ of order unity with Γ ∼ Td⁴ exp(−S3/Td); for an eV-scale transition the quoted condition is S3/Td ≃ 250.

Combine the thermal-equilibrium lower bound on λ with the imported neutrino-streaming constraint gs < 10⁻⁷/κ², the generated mass ms = gs vΨ, and m3 ≃ msκ². This produces a consistency bound tying the heaviest active-neutrino mass to phenomenological NEDE parameters.

Specialize imported general multiscalar results to obtain two- and four-loop beta functions; solve their zeros analytically where possible and numerically otherwise. Stability matrices and operator mixing determine sextic and quartic scaling data.

Graph/index counting bounds higher-loop contributions, making four loops complete at leading nontrivial 1/N or α. A gradient representation βa=Tab∂bU also organizes RG flows; its metric is positive definite for M>2 but degenerates at M=2.

Transform the background equations to redshift and luminosity-distance variables; compare predicted distance modulus μ=25+5 log10(d_L/Mpc) with observations. Additional diagnostics are matter-density positivity and the evolution of Λ_eff, Ω_K and expansion acceleration.

Numerically evolve the modified Friedmann equations using three phenomenological closures. Cases A and B borrow relations from ΛCDM; Case C imposes p_Λ=w0ρ_Λ. Each closure is examined with both present-day contortion roots, labeled branches 1 and 2.
Use the reviewed GVW superpotential, warped complex-structure metric, and the combined KS plus antibrane potential to determine shifts of the stabilized deformation modulus z.

Use the NS5 worldvolume potential and tadpole bookkeeping to track annihilation steps. Piecewise logarithmic NSNS flux profiles, radial rescalings, and matching at throat UV boundaries then describe the evolving geometry.

Differentiate pole locations, expand for λ|dj|/ρ≪1, propagate orders through nonlinear warp factors, and combine with inverse-metric orders. The full coframe variation and the printed inverse-sign inconsistency prevent treating this as a completely checked tensor computation.

Choose a metric identification and regulator, compute the quadratic tensor-variation norm, optionally normalize by total volume, and integrate along the path. The paper's normalized result additionally relies on a reported frame prescription.
Compute Ω from variations of the Lagrangian, supply compatible J, and integrate the resulting line element. In this paper the scaling component is imported from quiver quantum mechanics.

Promote static positions to slow collective coordinates, expand the action through O(v²), and read off the kinetic bilinear form. Constraints or integration of additional fields must be handled before comparing with a reduced moduli metric.

Construct scalar spaces from the centralizer quotient CE6(6)(GS)/CUSp(8)/Z2(GS). Compatible vector and hypermultiplet structures yield the factorisation M=MVT×MH; the cubic invariant on invariant generalised vectors supplies the very-special-real geometry.
Scan inequivalent Lie subgroups GS⊂USp(6) that introduce no additional spinor singlets; count GS singlets in 27* and 78 to determine vector/tensor and hypermultiplet content.

Compute singlet intrinsic torsion through generalised Lie derivatives of invariant tensors. Constant closure coefficients define a Leibniz bracket and embedding tensor. Because differential closure is assumed rather than solved, impose the Leibniz identity separately as a necessary algebraic restriction.

String-gas correlation functions are obtained from its partition function. DFT introduces ordinary and winding-dual spatial coordinates with a generalised metric; dependence on only one coordinate set recovers the usual metric, antisymmetric-tensor and dilaton supergravity sector.

Review linear cosmological perturbations using canonical Fourier modes satisfying vk''+[k²−z''/z]vk=0. The scalar background determines z, while tensor modes use z=a. The discussion connects sub-Hubble oscillations and super-Hubble squeezing to sensitivity to ultraviolet initial conditions.

Present three motivations for trans-Planckian censorship: maintaining a physical ultraviolet cutoff during expansion, an analogy with cosmic censorship, and bounds on sub-/super-Hubble entanglement entropy. These arguments are reviewed motivations rather than a proof of a quantum-gravity theorem.

Dimensionless functions F and G encode the potential slope and curvature. Their crossings with conjecture thresholds define φ• and φ‡; the authors combine these crossings and plot critical curves in the (c1,c2) plane for different µ/Mpl.

The construction uses a Kähler potential, a nonperturbative superpotential, and an F-term potential supplemented by D/U^b uplift. Angular coordinates diagonalize the Kähler matrix, followed by an expansion in the small brane-embedding ratio ε/µ.

For high-energy QCD instantons, lift fermion zero modes with complex dimension-six operators and a SUSY-breaking insertion, then match gauge-coupling running. For axion spectra, use Cholesky normalization and successive projections of hierarchically ordered instanton charges.

Estimate instanton amplitudes from divisor volumes, with action S=2πq·τ and leading BPS amplitudes proportional to (m3/2/V)|Aq|exp(−2πq·τ). Estimate Δθ using the first instanton whose charge, together with more dominant charges, spans the QCD charge.

Generate random triangulations using CYTools; choose rays through the stretched Kähler-cone tip, then dilate to match the observed infrared QCD coupling. Auxiliary scans along other rays reportedly give approximately unchanged results.

An ansatz with explicit angular dependence and eight unknown radial functions reduces the cohomogeneity-two PDE problem to ODEs. Algebraic relations and five-form self-duality reduce it further to two independent second-order ODEs, solved analytically with Mathematica; boundary conditions fix four integration constants.

Match weak brane perturbations of the background to long-wavelength deformations of the seed. The overlap profile contains flat, λ-background, ρc²-brane, and mixed λρc² terms, with limits recovering the background, linearized seed, and flat space.

Derive equilibrium relations from overlap-zone supergravity constraints and compute conserved charges using Gauss' law. Angular regularity fixes overlap integration constants; some B2 constants require regularity at the next mixed order λρc^4.

For exponential couplings, use the D-dimensional equations directly and introduce nonnegative curvature/flux master variables. Solve a linear system and bound its solutions by monotonicity on the nonnegative domain; external flux requires three cases around q=2/(n−1).

Dimensionally reduce the action, omit scalar derivative terms when locating constant-field extrema, and solve the metric and scalar equations order by order in a small Gauss–Bonnet parameter by expanding Q², internal curvature λ, and external curvature κ.

Mock observations assume four years with 75% efficiency, split into approximately 11.5-day segments, giving approximately 10^-6 Hz resolution. Gaussian signal and noise realizations are self-correlated, averaged and coarse-grained. PCA examples use the single TDI X stream.

PCA expands the signal in normalized Gaussians at pivot frequencies and fits linear signal and noise coefficients. The Fisher eigensystem defines components; components compatible with zero at 2σ are discarded before reconstructing signal and noise.

Template forecasts approximate the likelihood quadratically around injected fiducial parameters and use C=F^-1 for parameter covariance. Parameter scans report relative errors and SNR, with SNR²=T∫df(S_th/N_th)². This is a local forecast, not likelihood sampling or model selection.

Extract a,c through an effective curvature-squared gravitational action and anomaly relations. Static string corrections follow from unchanged off-shell BPS variations combined with corrected equations of motion; the near-horizon Lagrangian and reduced gravitational Chern–Simons term determine the sum and difference of 2d central charges.

Add the imported supersymmetric Weyl-squared and Ricci-scalar-squared invariants with real coefficients c1,c2. Fix conformal gauges and eliminate compensating/auxiliary fields perturbatively as Φ=Φ0+c_iφ_i+O(c_i²), while keeping the physical metric and gauge field off shell.

For rotating strings, use the off-shell 4d/5d reduction with a metric U(1) isometry and the known Weyl-squared reduction into Weyl-squared and T-log multiplets. A conjectured higher-derivative gravitational-block gluing rule supplies an entropy function for extremization; only nonzero q0 and angular momentum are retained in the illustrative result.
Tensoring with explicit auxiliary Hodge structures of weight one or two reduces odd-weight pairs and anti-self-dual classes to the even-weight self-dual theorem.

The proof imports R_an,exp-definability of the Weil-operator period map into an arithmetic quotient of G(R)/K. It constructs a definable bundle map from E and obtains the desired locus as a preimage of a universal self-dual locus.

Siegel sets, reduction of positive-definite quadratic forms, and stabilizer arithmetic quotients control the universal locus. Fixed positive self-intersection yields finitely many integral orthogonal-group orbits, using the cited lattice representation theorem.

Integrate the propagator-based mass consistency relation after changing variables to Δ. The digamma pair becomes a log-Gamma difference and negative-order polygamma sum. This reconstructs the scalar one-loop imaginary determinant subject to compatible branches and a fixed normalization.

Scalar boundary-generator traces localize at fixed points; hypergeometric solutions with outgoing conditions at both horizons determine QNMs. A Wronskian constructs the retarded propagator, while residue sums evaluate the imaginary determinant.

Heat-kernel regularization of spherical spectral sums, followed by a Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation and contour deformation, produces character integrals evaluated with Hurwitz zeta functions. The spinor calculation retains unpaired Dirac zero modes.

Apply ABS orientations, characteristic genera, extension of scalars, and integrated magnetic Bianchi identities. The six-dimensional Spin^c invariant calculation uses the signature theorem and a normal-bundle sequence.

Use the heuristic equivalence between an open-string vector-bundle description of a brane and its closed-string sourced/solitonic description to motivate matching their topological obstructions to decay.
Kodaira vanishing-order analysis, discriminant factorization, line-bundle degree counting and adjunction/Riemann–Roch constrain component types and special fibers.
Explicit base blowup chains replace e_(p−1) by e_(p−1)e_p and s by se_p, then divide (f,g,Δ) by (e_p⁴,e_p⁶,e_p¹²). Finite base changes u→u^k and blowdowns complete the canonicalization.

Apply imported definability theorems for arithmetic quotients and period maps. For variable flux, combine lattice orbits at fixed quadratic norm, arithmetic quotients of flux stabilizers, and pullback along a definable Weil-operator period map.

Use o-minimal definability, closure under projection and composition, cylindrical cell decomposition, and uniform bounds for definable families to translate geometric tameness into finiteness of disconnected choices and vacuum components.
KK reduction of Ricci and Gauss-Bonnet terms, covariant fourth derivatives of a polylogarithmic prepotential, and exponential Borcherds lifts separating modular from quasi-modular contributions.
Semistable degenerations, base changes and blowups of non-minimal Weierstrass fibers; string-junction monodromies; and an explicit genus-two Siegel modular mirror map for representative E7⊕E8 models.

Holographically renormalize the on-shell action using divergent and finite covariant counterterms. Construct four candidates by scheme choices and/or D1=1−j∂j and D3=1−(j/3)∂j; separately investigate a Legendre-transformed candidate.

Vary the DBI plus Wess–Zumino action with regularity imposed on both the embedding and C7. Allowed C7 gauge changes contribute boundary terms; interior regularity makes the variational principle well defined.

Numerically integrate the nonlinear embedding equation in Cartesian variables y(x), imposing terminating or space-filling interior conditions. Extract source and vev from boundary asymptotics; obtain analytic expansions near zero mass and infinite volume.

Use the functional RG flow k∂kΓk=(1/2)Tr[(Γk⁽²⁾+Rk)⁻¹k∂kRk], a truncation motivated by canonical power counting, and vertex projections to extract matter beta functions and anomalous dimensions. The computation uses a flat background and a Litim regulator.

Solve matter fixed-point equations, classify stability exponents over the gravitational parameter plane, and compare viable regions with a weak-gravity bound imported from a scalar-gravity truncation.

Eliminate the metric constraint variable, differentiate continuity, substitute Euler evolution, and solve the scalar equation algebraically. The EDS application uses constant α and neglects time-dependent response and drift under the stated quasistatic conditions.

Eliminate the nonoscillatory scalar offset algebraically in a quasistatic limit, then retain its order-c² contribution to dark matter growth. The operation does not replace the full evolution of freely oscillating or horizon-scale scalar perturbations.

Combine a one-dimensional Gaussian S_8 penalty with the baseline likelihood and rerun inference. Applicability to EDS is assumed from proximity to an EDE setting validated with an earlier DES release.

Solve the modified Einstein–Boltzmann system, sample the posterior, transform to physical parameters, and separately optimize likelihood. Different dataset branches have explicitly different model coverage, precision settings, and convergence thresholds.

Perturb c, compute the observable residual, adjust θ_i and z_c successively, and compare against a reoptimized model. For growth scans, hold H_0 fixed instead of the acoustic angle. Treat resulting degeneracies as local, model-dependent findings.

Modify CLASS EDE by adding coupled pressureless matter, supplying scalar stresses and exchange equations to the synchronous Einstein solver, and retaining a small uncoupled CDM species to define the gauge. Consistent field units are required for the displayed scalar equations.

Initialize the scalar in slow roll and perturbations adiabatically, enforce the energy budget, and use iterative shooting for potential parameters and initial matter density. The source does not provide iteration tolerances or failure-handling rules.

Vary the homogeneous and perturbative scalar action, evaluate total conservation, and insert the scalar equations to determine matter exchange terms. The paper applies this operation to a canonical EDE field and scalar-dependent fermion mass.

Sequential parameter shifts distinguish a localized acoustic correction from a damping-scale correction. Posterior correlations provide the paper's numerical confirmation of the proposed compensation direction.

For mutually local D(−1)/D1 instantons, use the contact potential χ to encode corrections and K≈−logχ as an asymptotic metric description. Extract mirror special Lagrangian cycle volumes from calibrated periods and their large-complex-structure scaling.

Compare brane tensions and KK scales under circle reduction. Translate known IIB hypermultiplet corrections through mirror symmetry and the identification of five-dimensional M-theory and four-dimensional IIA hypermultiplet moduli spaces.

Complementary calculations use relativistic string/membrane limits, direct and double dimensional reduction, and the Seiberg–Witten map. RR Buscher rules follow from matching Chern–Simons couplings, with infinitesimal Stueckelberg transformations supplying an additional consistency check.

First-order parent actions treat F as independent and impose F=dA with antisymmetric Lagrange multipliers. Integrating out A and then the nondynamical field strength yields dual variables; for D2 the dual scalar becomes the eleventh coordinate.

The search treats 18 integer wrapping numbers as a constrained Diophantine system. Products A=−n1n2n3, B=n1l2l3, C=l1n2l3 and D=l1l2n3, together with their n↔l counterparts, organize sign branches allowed by supersymmetry.

Recursive reductions solve zero products by branching, nonzero integer products by finite factorization, full-rank linear systems, and linear-inequality subsystems with finitely many integer solutions. The authors invoke polyhedral tests, including Fourier–Motzkin elimination, to identify the latter.

When those reductions stop, remaining sign choices and nonlinear supersymmetry inequalities eliminate residual cases. A computer program implements the search; the text supplies an example rejected because a required ratio of positive supersymmetry parameters becomes negative.

Project the functional RG flow onto retained interaction monomials and wave-function terms, using a spectrally adjusted regulator with a Litim-type shape function. Employ a flat background and linear metric split gμν=δμν+hμν.

Track shifted Gaussian fixed points numerically until their couplings become complex; compare the resulting boundary with gravitational fixed points computed from imported background-field beta functions. Supplement finite-NV searches with an analytical NV→∞ limit.

Apply Euler's theorem to ln𝒱, differentiate once, and use the relation between real and complex derivatives to derive inverse-metric contractions. This avoids constructing the complete inverse metric for an arbitrary number of Kähler moduli.

Extract the radial scaling of a positive potential and use the logarithmic metric to bound its full multifield gradient. In this paper the operation closes the inverse-homogeneous-correction inequality even when its mixed term has an unrestricted sign.

Represent the antibrane uplift through a nilpotent chiral multiplet X in four-dimensional supergravity. Match a local off-shell expansion of the induced superpotential to ten-dimensional input, add the nonperturbative term, and inspect the scalar potential through an illustrative example and a partial parameter scan.

Use previously obtained linearized ten-dimensional fluctuations around KS to calculate the induced three-form components, integrate the GVW superpotential, and numerically evaluate flux integrals determining conifold and axio-dilaton F-terms.
Solve the pointwise inequality by tuning a and setting b=1-a. When a is fixed below 1/(1-h), use the decreasing function f^q to determine whether any q>2 exists.

Transform a nonminimally coupled scalar theory to Einstein gravity, then integrate the scalar kinetic coefficient. The input kinetic function must be retained because different choices produce different canonical maps.

Invert the scalar-tilt and tensor-ratio relations to evaluate the two conjectures at one canonical field point. This operation requires mutually consistent observables from the same approximation and parameter choice.
Differentiate, integrate, invert, and normalize a canonical scalar potential. Retain the approximation order used in the field solution before interpreting subleading observable coefficients.

A continuously rotating half-wave plate modulates sky polarization at 4f_HWP, permits polarization measurement with a single detector, and suppresses 1/f noise and leakage caused by mismatches between detector pairs. HWP-induced polarization effects remain part of the instrument trade study.

Expand temperature in spherical harmonics and Q+iU in spin-weighted harmonics, then form angular auto- and cross-power spectra. Statistical isotropy motivates angular-separation-dependent correlations; near-Gaussianity makes two-point statistics especially informative.

Process time-ordered data into frequency maps, separate physical components, and compare CMB statistics with theoretical predictions. Forecasts propagate foreground residuals and instrumental systematic effects into r, with marginalization used for debiasing.

Conjugate the type-IIB SL(2,R) action by the classical mirror-map diffeomorphism. Identify X_e=P_0 and X_h=D−D_1; prove X_f Killing by reducing its Lie derivative to H⊂N and propagating vanishing using known Killing flows and homogeneous linear ODEs.

Describe twistor geometry through HK/QK correspondence and conification: Z is a holomorphic C× quotient of the HK cone, and a degree-two homogeneous holomorphic one-form descends to a line-bundle-valued contact form.

Introduce logarithmic sources for charge-n insertions and normalize their correlators by the defect expectation value. Position-space cutoffs extract logarithmic anomalous dimensions. For two defects, isolate the interaction action after removing the separate single-defect contributions.

Rescale fields and couplings so the effective action carries an overall n, then evaluate the path integral by a large-n saddle. Solve the sourced classical equations perturbatively in the scaled bulk couplings while retaining the defect coupling in the selected semiclassical approximation.

Evaluate on-shell actions using Green functions and transverse Fourier integrals. Extract defect-coupling counterterms and beta functions with dimensional regularization and minimal subtraction; regulate the longitudinal extent by T for lines and V for surfaces.

Expand φ(z), V(φ), and H(z), solve background equations order by order, and eliminate potential coefficients. Random scalar profiles passing hierarchy cuts define perturbative models whose best fits are compared with ΛCDM; unstable KGB fits are discarded afterward.

Fit approximately 10,000 DESI-forecast BAO mock realizations with CPL and flat ΛCDM; repeat below z=1 with CPL and w(z)=w0+wa z. Selected mocks undergo MCMC marginalization to assess representative H0 uncertainties.

Analyze linear scalar metric and fluid perturbations subject to the unimodular constraint. Use the compatible comoving gauge v + B = 0 and the gauge-invariant combination ℛ = ψ - ℋ(v + B), derive its mode equation, and adopt canonical quantization of M = zℛ with a Bunch-Davies vacuum.

Parameterize the background using Hubble flow functions, derive conditions on Q and its logarithmic derivative, and reconstruct Q from a chosen ε1(N). A phenomenological two-parameter example is continued through radiation and matter eras using continuity equations and numerical integration.

Balance the anti-D3 uplift against the AdS depth, eliminate W0 through the higher F-term control condition, and impose the warping correction bound. The resulting charge equation is solved using the W−1 branch of the Lambert W function.

Estimate the warping correction by reducing a ten-dimensional R⁴ interaction to the four-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert term. A Poisson-equation estimate with six-dimensional Green-function behavior gives typical bulk warp variations of order N/V^(2/3).

Derive the non-backreacted uplift from the KS geometry, retaining the additive volume-dependent warp-factor contribution. The resulting uplift scales as exp[−8πK/(3gs M)]/[(gs M²)V^(4/3)], with a specified numerical prefactor subject to geometric normalization assumptions.
Encode the background equations in F(H) = H² + Σ(n≥3)α(n)H^(2n): 3F(H) = κρ and −(Ḣ/H)F′(H) = κ(ρ + P). This reduces the FLRW evolution to an equation for the Hubble parameter.

Numerically evolve the background from present-day initial conditions into the past. Compare H(z) and supernova magnitudes with a GR ΛCDM reference and plot the binned Pantheon sample; the reported supernova agreement is qualitative.

Choose factorially weighted coefficient families that resum into exponential functions. The general family uses fixed integers p, q, s with q = ks; the explicit example takes p = 4, q = 2, s = 1 and contains competing exponential terms multiplying H⁸.

Construct a four-dimensional Einstein-frame action and a radion potential V(R) = Vtr(R) + V1L(R). The tree term is proportional to Λ4/R; the one-loop Casimir term sums particle contributions involving modified Bessel functions K5/2.

Expand the five-dimensional scalar curvature while retaining derivatives of gμν along θ. Vary the tensor component and separate variables to obtain a four-dimensional Einstein equation and a nonlinear ordinary differential equation for χ.

For KK fields, expand the Λ4 = 0 profile through order κ² at small κ. Solve the resulting mode equations using even Hermite polynomials and confluent hypergeometric functions, imposing equal endpoint values.

Couple higher-form currents to background gauge fields, determine their mixed transformations and invariant field strengths, and use the required ordering of symmetry-emergence scales to constrain charged-particle masses.

Use string-worldsheet anomaly inflow to identify charged excitations; diagonalize supergravity kinetic matrices and dualize form fields to compare gauge-coupling scalings with Chern-Simons interactions.
Parametrize solutions by entropy S, temperature T and non-extremality c=2ST; examine horizon scalar profiles and charge-scaling limits to connect thermodynamic boundaries to moduli-space distance.
Use non-extremal STU I-functions and extremal attractor equations, then infer candidate towers from the horizon internal volume: mKK=Vh^(-1/6), mwind=Vh^(1/6), and distance approximately |log Vh|.

Analyze turnaround slices first, then evaluate the conditions using full FRW solutions. Where conditions overlap, establish examples at turnaround by choosing R with the same size and location as I; full-spacetime exclusion checks are presented graphically.

Use entropy subadditivity, strong subadditivity, quantum extremality, and competition with empty or whole-universe candidates to derive reference-independent necessary conditions. Reduce these conditions to entropy, area, and radial derivative inequalities for spherical regions.

Expand k perturbatively in a running dimensionless coupling α_g and solve dα_g/dlnτ=b₁α_g²+… . Leading-log resummation retains all orders in α_g lnτ while higher powers of the small coupling remain suppressed.

Compute the supergravity potential and kinetic metric, extremize the modulus at fixed inflaton, and estimate slow-roll evolution along the resulting trough. Constrained superfields encode antibrane tension and the large-separation Coulomb interaction.

Define a radius-dependent effective charge q(r) through correlators containing a symmetry operator surrounding a charged operator. Strong breaking occurs when its logarithmic radial variation, normalized by the infrared charge q∞, becomes O(1); rsym ∼ Λ⁻¹.

Use perturbative propagator self-energies, screening potentials, branch-cut integrals and Fourier transforms to extract nonanalytic charge variation. The magnetic calculation instead evaluates integrated current two-point functions; scalar shift breaking is obtained from Yukawa-loop corrections.

Uses slow-roll potential expressions ε1=(1−λ)(V′/V)²/2 and ε2=−2(1−λ)[V″/V−(V′/V)²], together with ns=1−2ε1−ε2 and r=16(1−λ)ε1. These are formulas adopted by the paper, without independent verification in this pass.

Inverts the model expressions r(N) and ns(N) to eliminate the e-fold variable, then constructs relations between C1, C2 and r, ns. Plots of these relations and of the C2–C1 plane supply the authors' asserted permissible regions.

Introduce non-BPS deviations X_I=q_I−Z_e C_{IJK}t^Jt^K and X^I=p^I−Z_m t^I. Solve their orthogonality constraints first, then determine an overall factor from contracted attractor equations; vanishing deviations identify BPS points.

Reduce to t=x/y and electric or magnetic charge ratios. Rational inverse functions q(t), p(t), monotonicity, Descartes’ rule and numerical roots determine solution multiplicities and allowed Kähler-cone intervals.
Extremize electric V_e=(3/2)Z_e²−(1/2)C^{IJ}q_Iq_J and magnetic V_m=3Z_m²−2C_{IJ}p^Ip^J using Lagrange multipliers enforcing C_{IJK}t^It^Jt^K=1. Here C_{IJ}=C_{IJK}t^K and C^{IJ} is its inverse.

The historical construction uses Euclidean path integrals to specify quantum states. Earlier joint work on black-hole radiance employed complex time and Euclidean geometry, providing a methodological precedent rather than a cosmological derivation reproduced in this essay.

Early cosmological predictions used semiclassical algorithms posited by analogy with nonrelativistic WKB. Subsequent work developed Decoherent or Consistent Histories quantum mechanics to formulate cosmological predictions beyond laboratory measurement situations.

Analytic large-N bootstrap combines crossing, supersymmetric Ward identities, Lorentzian inversion and Mellin-space analyticity. Localization or protected sectors fix remaining constants at the first few derivative orders; the large-radius limit relates correlators to flat-space amplitudes.

Numerical bootstrap tests unitarity and crossing of four-point functions through semidefinite programming, supplemented by localization data. Mixed correlators and additional protected integrated correlators are proposed to sharpen islands and isolate theories with a single stress tensor.

Polyakov–Mellin bootstrap expands in crossing-symmetric exchange Witten diagrams with contact contributions. Constraints remove spurious double-trace contributions, expressed as vanishing Mellin pole residues and related to dispersion relations.

Extracted spectra are fitted with response redistribution included, using emcee MCMC in 3ML. Astrophysical spectra comprise a cutoff power law for unresolved sources, a power law for IC, positron-annihilation components and nuclear lines with adjustable normalizations.

Spatial templates are forward-convolved with the energy- and aspect-dependent coded-mask response. Expected detector/pointing count patterns plus instrumental background are fitted with a Poisson maximum likelihood independently in each energy bin, before spectral modeling.

BlackHawk v1.2 supplies primary Hawking photon spectra. Four GALPROP v56 IC morphologies test foreground systematics; the PBH spatial template uses the line-of-sight density integral, factorized from the mass-dependent emission spectrum.

Use three-point rank-one spinor factorizations and reference spinors, Grassmann delta functions at four points, and double-copy products with little-group projections. Compare resulting three-vector amplitudes with the supergravity cubic coupling to extract C_IJK.

Represent supersymmetry by fermionic oscillators built from unconstrained Grassmann variables and derivatives; package states into on-shell superfields and extract components by Grassmann differentiation. Bosonic auxiliary variables dress and symmetrize little-group indices.

Factorize antisymmetric momentum bispinors using their on-shell rank: two for null momentum and four for massive momentum. Construct massive spinors from p=k+m²q, with k and q null; explicit rational momentum parametrizations avoid square roots.

Solve the trace equation and xx field equation using odd R(x)=r1x+r3x³+… and even S(x)=s0(1+s2x²+…) expansions. Rescale to universal interior functions, integrate from a small positive coordinate, and shoot for smooth matching to Schwarzschild asymptotics.

Apply Tolman redshift and integrate thermal densities: S22=(2π²/45)N T∞³V22 and U22=(3/4)T∞S22. The effective volume is the integral of 4πS(x)² over the trapped interior, so R cancels from these thermodynamic expressions.
Use ds²=(R²/S²)(−dt²+dx²)+R²dΩ², where x is the tortoise coordinate. The conformally related metric is −dt²+dx²+S²dΩ², separating the roles of the areal radius R and the optical length scale S.

Differentiate the ordinary F-term potential V=e^K(K^{i j̄}D_iW D_j̄W̄−3|W|²) twice at a supersymmetric extremum. Use the F-term equations, no-scale identities and simplified superpotential derivatives to obtain saxion and axion Hessians.

Translate scalar masses using Δ(Δ−d)=m²R_AdS² with d=3. For complex-structure saxions, apply N=1 superconformal multiplet constraints to choose between the two roots compatible with the stated unitarity bound.

Write the AdS-normalized Hessians as H_M=9K+2L and H_A=5K+3L, where L is rank one. Physical masses are eigenvalues of 2K^−1H; no-scale identities give eigenvalues 0 with multiplicity n_K and 13 once for K^−1L, avoiding explicit flux-dependent vacuum solutions.

Measure component/total power spectra and Rockstar halo concentrations. Compute stacked excess surface density around the 20,000 most massive halos using all particles in cylinders of line-of-sight height 100 h⁻¹ Mpc; estimate observational discrimination through rescaled DES Y1 covariance matrices.

Sample each relic speed by inverse-CDF sampling of its background velocity distribution, choose a random direction, and add that velocity to the gravitational peculiar velocity. The procedure permits different negligibly interacting relic distributions.

Modified Gadget2 evolves two particle species. CLASS supplies component linear spectra and growth rates at z=99; NGenIC generates Zel’dovich initial conditions. An overall initial-spectrum rescaling compensates for radiation being included in CLASS but omitted from N-body evolution.

Encode wrapped NS5-branes as GLSM anomaly sources, canceled using logarithmic FI terms and an antisymmetric counterterm. Exponentiated parameters obey qᵢ(z)=q̄ᵢ(z/z₀)^(eⁱ); the mirror map incorporates worldsheet-instanton corrections.

Identify string cores with intersections of the profile curve and singular divisors. Compute global energy through Kähler-form integrals, constrain deficit angles using monodromy products, and use Stokes' theorem to argue that cycle area is independent of its representative.

Define EQGs by δL_reduced/δf=0 for constant lapse and every f(r), making the reduced Lagrangian a total derivative. The studied quasitopological subclass has an integrated algebraic metric equation. Electromagnetic dualization uses an algebraic field-strength relation and a Legendre transform.

Use conformal-collider energy fluxes to determine the current correlator structure. Map spherical charged Rényi entropies to thermal entropy on the hyperbolic cylinder, evaluate them from grand-potential differences, and expand twist observables around n=1, μ=0.

Compute black-hole entropy with Iyer–Wald, free energies through the on-shell Euclidean action and effective asymptotic boundary terms, and shear viscosity through the horizon pole-residue prescription for a transverse metric perturbation.

Analytic linear functionals can certify saturation of bootstrap bounds. Tauberian theorems constrain averaged heavy-operator data, while thermal bootstrap equations impose compatibility of the OPE with periodicity around the thermal circle.

Conformal dispersion relations follow from inversion plus partial-wave expansion, or from Cauchy's theorem for Mellin amplitudes. Associated dispersive functionals have double zeros at double-twist locations, apart from finitely many Regge trajectories; dispersion also motivates Polyakov-Regge block expansions.

The lightcone bootstrap analyzes crossing near null separation, converting dominance by the identity and low-twist operators in one channel into large-spin spectral information in another. The Lorentzian inversion formula extracts partial-wave coefficients from an integrated double commutator.

Linearized 5D Einstein equations are combined with a trace-free perturbation gauge, brane bending l = l0 + ζ(x), coordinate changes fixing the brane position, and jump/mean-value equations across the brane.

A near-horizon Rindler expansion estimates the locally measured Hawking temperature. Radial null travel to a Planck-distance layer estimates the lifetime, while massive radial geodesics and coordinate transformations probe departures from FLRW isotropy.

The author studies the positive-tension brane action S = −σ∫√−g and a static extremization argument, then diagonalizes near-brane coordinates by foliating with nearby embeddings labeled by their de Sitter length.

The transport calculation uses a radial integral for the shear diffusion coefficient and η/s = TD. Retarded correlators, a Kubo expression and a shear dispersion expansion motivate the hydrodynamic interpretation; the printed prescriptions contain unresolved inconsistencies.

The covariant Abbott-Deser-Tekin method linearizes gravitational equations around an AdS reference background and converts the conserved current associated with a timelike Killing vector into a boundary charge. The authors import earlier four-/six-derivative work and extend the calculation to eight derivatives.

Corrected metric ansätze and Hawking temperatures are evaluated perturbatively. An auxiliary horizon parameter r̃ is introduced so that corrected and uncorrected mass/charge comparisons are performed at the same boundary temperature.

Analyze linear electromagnetic dispersion relations for Maxwellian species using the plasma dispersion function Z and its warm/cold expansions. The search emphasizes purely growing modes, with analytic approximations for unmagnetized warm, warm-cold and cold limits.

Numerical roots are sought by minimizing |D(k,ω)|² with Nelder–Mead. Analytic solutions normally supply initial guesses; the magnetized Bullet Cluster search instead starts near ω=iΩχ. The authors explicitly warn that root finding can depend on the algorithm and need not identify the fastest mode.

Decompose the scalar potential into RR, NS–NS/geometric, and local/tadpole pieces with explicit volume, complex-structure, and dilaton dependence. First apply volume–dilaton extremization and Hessian conditions, then include the remaining moduli; passing the two-field test is only necessary.

Use axionic flux combinations, analytic saxion extremization without D-terms, and numerical polynomial extremization in rescaled variables with D-terms. Hessian eigenvalues classify the reported extrema, while flux scaling estimates guide benchmark choices.

Dimensionally reduce the action, use Bianchi identities to rewrite source contributions, and estimate the reported Einstein-frame scalar potential by powers of n. Excise neighborhoods of the O6 loci and retain boundary terms to expose cutoff-dependent singular contributions.

Derive localized string-frame Einstein, dilaton, and flux/Bianchi equations, compare them with smeared equations, and expand around the smeared solution using a large flux parameter n. The method uses equations of motion rather than supersymmetry conditions.

Reduce the linearized source corrections to Poisson equations with source equal to smeared density minus localized density. Solve with torus Fourier Green functions βi; their derivatives determine F2 corrections. Harmonic F4 corrections are adjusted so the integrated F6 Bianchi identity requires no additional sources.

Use normalized geodesic conjugation/equivalence for UV classification and gradient conjugation/equivalence for IR classification. Apply the imported surface uniformization theorem together with conformal invariance of gradient orbits to obtain the two-field reduction.

Rescale cosmological curves and their geometric ODE; expand the reduced Hubble function to obtain formal UV and IR asymptotic expansions. A Riemannian exponential-map formulation describes higher corrections, but technical details of their construction are deferred.

Helicity-dependent electromagnetic propagation is treated with a WKB approximation. A photon Boltzmann equation and visibility-function integrals handle finite-duration last scattering and reionisation when a single rotation angle is inadequate.

Vacuum tensor modes are quantised using the quadratic Einstein–Hilbert action, canonical normalisation and positive-frequency sub-Hubble matching. Slowly varying gauge-field production admits Whittaker-function solutions; transverse-traceless stress supplies sourced tensors.

Spin-2 spherical-harmonic decomposition defines E/B multipoles and angular spectra. Joint modelling of CMB and Galactic foreground EB correlations separates instrumental angle miscalibration from cosmic rotation, subject to assumptions about intrinsic EB.

The inflaton and Friedmann equations determine the background; numerical Mukhanov–Sasaki evolution supplies the scalar spectrum through USR. The CMB spectral index is extracted by linear regressions around 52.5–53.5 e-folds before inflation ends rather than a slow-roll formula.

PBH abundances are estimated from a Gaussian curvature-perturbation collapse tail, then redshifted to a present dark-matter fraction. Numerical examples use the peak scalar-spectrum amplitude in this estimate; this is not a full PBH mass-function calculation.

A second-order Einstein equation with a transverse-traceless projection and radiation-era scalar transfer function gives the induced tensor spectrum. The numerical scalar spectrum is inserted into the double convolution for present-day GW energy density and compared with interferometer sensitivity curves.

Use the imported one-loop-exact super-Schwarzian partition function, then Fourier/Laplace decomposition into charge sectors and energies. Killing-spinor bilinears and spinorial Lie derivatives determine the near-horizon superalgebra.

Identify the effective theory from the near-horizon super-isometry and the low-temperature on-shell action, including ensemble boundary terms and a sum over integer holonomy shifts. Match these to an N=2 super-Schwarzian rather than deriving a complete dimensional reduction.

For AdS3, modular transformations of extended N=2 vacuum characters and integer spectral flow implement the additional saddle sum and charge quantization. The resulting near-extremal density matches the super-Schwarzian form; universality requires the stated large-central-charge or large-spin/twist-gap regimes.

Use the nineteen-node Extended Dynkin Diagram of the Narain lattice. Deleting nodes identifies candidate enhancement diagrams, and imposing pR=0 for retained nodes locates their moduli-space loci. The two extended E8 diagrams share an imaginary root.

Construct KK-dressed Cartan and root currents J_n^a(z)=J^a(z)e^{iny(z)}, including cocycles. Take R→∞ in their OPEs and use contour integrals of Laurent zero modes to read the affine commutators and central generator.

Dimensionally reduce heterotic supergravity to the nine-dimensional Einstein frame, diagonalize dilaton/radion kinetic terms, and normalize gauge fields to quantized charges. Compute long-range probe forces from linearized gravitational, scalar and Abelian gauge exchange.

Evaluate the q functional integral semiclassically, then apply Picard–Lefschetz contour deformation to the positive-real lapse integral. Retain the classical q solution that avoids interior zeros; select steepest-descent contours on which Im(iS) is constant.

Decompose scalar perturbations into S³ harmonics, integrate out nondynamical fields and constraints in first-order form, and isolate a canonical gauge-invariant scalar. After Wick rotation, analyze a Schrödinger operator using asymptotics, perturbation theory and finite differences.

Implement fixed-flux amplitudes in the axion description through a Fourier transform over boundary axion values. The lapse integral yields a modified Bessel function; its asymptotic expression and a further saddle approximation are used after dropping prefactors.

Use canonical hyperbolic coordinates and leading Taylor expansions of the extended potential: linear at noncritical ends and quadratic at critical points. Integrate the end-orbit Pfaffian equations using the lower incomplete gamma function γ₂(v)=1−(1+v)e^(−v).

Numerically integrate the second-order cosmological equations with initial velocity on the effective gradient-flow shell. Examples use truncated local potentials and fixed normalizations, including M₀=V(c)=λ₂(c)=1 for critical-point computations.

Obtain equations by sequential weak-gravity, slow-motion and nonrelativistic limits, with the latter two applied only to the ordinary fluid in the general scalar formulation. Use uniform-expansion gauge for the gravitational constraints.
In MHD, combine Ohm's law with modified Gauss and Ampère equations to eliminate electric charge/current variables and derive a magnetic induction equation and effective fluid force.

Apply the Klein decomposition and time averaging to the oscillating massive scalar, followed by the Madelung density/phase transformation. Analyze density perturbations and resolve the linear magnetic field into circular-polarization Fourier modes.

Use weak-coupling and large-volume expansions, analytic volume extremization and second derivatives, followed by numerical minimization in the three tα directions. Inspect Hessian eigenvalues for selected uplifted examples.

Parametrize volume-dependent one-loop effects by f(V), compute the corrected Kähler metric, and invert it through four auxiliary coefficient equations. Derive no-scale-breaking identities and a scalar-potential master formula, then add KK, winding and F⁴ terms.

Separate the minimally coupled charged Klein-Gordon equation into frequency, spatial momentum and radial factors. Solve the HSV radial equation using Whittaker functions at zero temperature and hypergeometric functions in the finite-temperature throat.

Extract asymptotic coefficients, form the retarded correlator as Bk/Ak and identify candidate quasinormal frequencies through its poles. For KNA, use the cited gamma-function correlator and a quadratic near-horizon expansion of the metric function.

Construct electric character and magnetic cocharacter lattices from zero-asymptotic-charge physical junctions modulo global integer null loops. Extract the non-Abelian quotient as Z=Jfrac^(N,mag)/Jint^(N,mag), and the quotient involving Abelian factors from Z′=PA(Jphys^mag)/JA^mag.

Represent junctions by prong lattices with a symmetric bilinear pairing, conserved asymptotic (p,q) charge and SL(2,Z) monodromy. Use branch-cut crossings and Hanany-Witten transitions to change presentations and express loops in a prong basis.

Compare junction lattices with the imported heterotic Narain lattice (−E8)²⊕U² and CHL Mikhailov lattice (−E8)⊕U⊕U(2). Identify loop imaginary roots of affine stacks with towers of BPS states and KK momenta in decompactification limits.

For N=8, vanishing spin-1/2 supersymmetry variations sets A₂=0. E7(7)/SU(8) identities then relate the gravitino mass to gauge charges. Moving to a purely electric frame and normalizing the vectors yields the corresponding charge bound. Partial-breaking examples use consistency of truncated supersymmetry transformations and N=2 multiplet arrangements.

The vectors and charge matrices are projected onto a selected U(1) direction and its orthogonal complement using the kinetic matrix. After fixing the gauge coupling normalization, negative definiteness of the inverse kinetic matrix bounds the full negative vacuum energy by the selected charge contribution.

For N=2, the supersymmetry condition PΛˣfᵢΛ=0 and special Kähler identities express the gravitino mass and vacuum energy using moment maps and the inverse vector kinetic matrix. A charge matrix combines the special Kähler and quaternionic moment maps.

The cosmological translation adds the axion to a specified ΛCDM background with Ω0,M=0.31, Ω0,R=9×10⁻⁵ and ΩΛ=0.69. Starting at rest with χ0=(π−0.01)f, the author fits the axion density evolution to a phenomenological EDE interpolation to obtain ac and fEDE.

The instanton action is related to the potential amplitude through mχ²=ΛUV⁴e^(−S)/feff². Substitution into the axion WGC produces an n-independent inequality involving feff and a logarithm of ΛUV⁴/(feff²mχ²). The bound is evaluated for representative EDE parameters.

The scalar equation is rewritten in redshift and numerically integrated on a prescribed fluid-dominated background. The authors track both the scalar displacement and its effective energy density relative to the cosmic fluid, comparing the cubic model with its quadratic counterpart.

Scalar fluctuations are separated as δϕ=u(r)e^(−iωt)Yℓm/r. Tortoise coordinates produce a Schrödinger-type radial equation. A negative integral of its effective potential supplies a sufficient condition for an unstable mode; the quoted mass/coupling restrictions use the spherically symmetric mode.

Gaussian-process regression reconstructs H(z), with H0 obtained by extrapolation to z = 0. Cosmic chronometers infer H(z) from differential ages of massive, passively evolving galaxies; reconstruction depends on covariance assumptions.

Bayesian evidence and Bayes factors compare cosmological models, including shared-parameter versus experiment-specific parameter models. Assessment must consider overall fit and parameter freedom, since reducing a tension metric alone can conceal a poor fit.

Parameter inference combines theoretical spectra from Einstein–Boltzmann solvers such as CLASS and CAMB with MCMC or nested sampling. Repeated solver evaluations become computationally expensive for many parameters or slow parameters.

Expand observables in Virasoro conformal blocks, average OPE products using Wick contractions, and evaluate heavy-state integrals semiclassically. The Cardy density and DOZZ-related universal OPE function serve as modular and fusion crossing kernels.

Construct hyperbolic quotient geometries and cut-and-glue handles; obtain actions through Brown–York stress tensors, holographic Ward identities and monodromy. One-loop comparisons use Selberg zeta functions and imported holomorphic factorization results for functional determinants.

Construct the complete intersection, form its associated double cover and identify that double cover with the Jacobian because it already has a section. Analyze the resulting global defining equation, with a Weierstrass transformation used for discriminant and fiber calculations.

The Mordell–Weil argument restricts sections to the K3 fiber, asserts an inclusion into its known Z4⊕Z4 group, and exhibits at least sixteen sections through factorizations and rearrangements of the double-cover equation.

Gauge algebra is inferred from discriminant components, Kodaira fiber types and splitting. Matter is inferred using collision symmetry and gravitational anomaly counting. Stable degeneration is analyzed through collisions of singular fibers and an imported classification of extremal K3 surfaces.

Use GaPP to reconstruct H(z) and H′(z) with squared-exponential and Matérn ν=9/2 covariance kernels. The GP is a distribution over functions conditioned on observations; correlation length and fluctuation amplitude are kernel hyperparameters.

Construct the displayed central V(φ) curve from the reconstructed means of V(z) and φ(z). Combine their lower and upper 2σ bounds to obtain what the authors call possible maximum error bounds, then compare illustrative potential curves with these reconstructions.

Express ρφ=3H²−3H0²Ω0(1+z)³ and Pφ=2(1+z)HH′−3H², then obtain V=(ρφ−Pφ)/2. Reconstruct the field using the squared-field-derivative relation in Eq. (14) and the first-order redshift finite difference in Eq. (17).

Full-crossing null constraints sharpen coefficient bounds; semidefinite programming optimizes them. Numerical S-matrix bootstrap additionally uses full partial-wave unitarity and truncated crossing-symmetric amplitude expansions.

Scattering phase shifts and Eisenbud–Wigner time delays probe causality. Infrared causality compares low-energy delay with the background Shapiro delay: ΔT_net > ΔT_g − O(1)ω^(-1), retaining finite temporal resolution.

Cauchy-contour fixed-t dispersion relations connect low-energy derivatives to absorptive parts. Partial-wave Legendre/Gegenbauer positivity and positive-spectral moment/Hankel constructions generate linear and nonlinear bounds.

Tomita–Takesaki modular theory defines continuum relative entropy and modular flow using operator algebras. Gaussian free theories admit correlation-matrix methods whose spectra determine entanglement quantities.

Simulation methods include matrix product states, coarse-graining or open-system constructions that reduce entanglement generation, and MERA/DMERA representations adapted into state-preparation circuits.

Replica path integrals compute integer Rényi entropies, followed by analytic continuation toward n=1. Twist-operator correlators in two dimensions and codimension-two replica defects in higher dimensions enable CFT, bootstrap and OPE methods.

Reviewed lattice methods include gradient flow, multiple lattice spacings and above-physical pion masses followed by physical-mass interpolation. Further targets include finite-temperature topological susceptibility and small-instanton contributions to quark masses and the NLO chiral Lagrangian.

Cross-correlating hadronic, nuclear, atomic and molecular EDMs can distinguish a pure-θ source from additional dimension-six CP-violating operators. Microscopic-to-observable matching requires improved lattice, hadronic and nuclear calculations.
Axion-substructure studies combine semi-analytic structure formation, N-body simulations and analytic models of stellar encounters and tidal disruption.

Thermal phase transitions are estimated through gravitational instantons connecting a bubble of RS geometry to the surrounding AdS black-hole phase. A light-radion effective theory approximates the bubble action and tunneling exponent.

Double holography translates island formation into competing BCFT OPE exchange channels and permits entanglement phase diagrams to be studied with classical bulk gravity. Graviton masses are analyzed through bulk fluctuations or boundary stress-tensor anomalous dimensions.

Five-dimensional simplified models use KK towers and cascade decays to generate event shapes with few parameters. Warped curvature permits slightly off-threshold decays with randomly oriented momenta; varying a scalar mass interpolates between event topologies.

Tests the AdS distance conjecture through families of effective theories: homogeneous rescaling of all neutrino masses at fixed cosmological constant, with 10⁻⁴ < λ < 1, and non-homogeneous scanning that changes only the lightest neutrino mass.

Uses an imported one-loop radion potential containing the cosmological-constant contribution and particle Casimir sums with modified Bessel function K2, spin-statistics signs, winding number n, and twist factor cos(2πnθp). Numerical analysis varies the twist and lightest neutrino mass to locate positive-energy minima, AdS minima, and runaway behavior.

Review heuristic black-hole arguments for global-charge violation and entropy bounds, together with concrete mechanisms for exponentially suppressed symmetry breaking: gauge instantons, higher-dimensional gauge fields and nonlocal worldsheet effects.

Combine conjectural charge-to-mass bounds with species counting and weak-coupling towers; use a BF/Stueckelberg description to relate vector masses to charged strings. Entropy arguments compare field-theory volume scaling with gravitational area scaling and collapse limits.

Control tools include coupling and inverse-radius expansions, large-N/large-D expansions, instanton calculus, worldsheet methods, rigidity results, supersymmetric constraints, integrability, and numerical methods. Applicability depends on the construction.

The cosmological bootstrap uses singularities, symmetry differential equations, perturbative cutting rules, and conformal partial-wave decompositions. Analytic continuation to Euclidean AdS with doubled fields provides another calculational tool; the relation between the two stated unitarity constraints remains incompletely understood.

Computational topology enumerates Euclidean D3-brane superpotential terms. Mirror symmetry and period computations permit flux choices canceling polynomial superpotential terms, leaving exponentially small corrections balanced in a racetrack; CYTools is reported to extend these computations.

Reviews two descriptions of virtual-dyon potentials: integrating out axion-dependent dyon masses and summing Coleman–Weinberg-type contributions, or integrating closed monopole trajectories with winding in a compact collective-coordinate direction.

Thermal friction is related to the sphaleron rate through fluctuation–dissipation in the transport limit, with Γ_sph = 2 f_a² T Υ. Coupled scalar and dark-radiation evolution equations describe dissipation and radiation production.

Revisits classical minimization of axion-gradient plus electric-field energy around a minimally charged monopole, imposing spherical symmetry and a fixed asymptotic axion background. The quoted profile and energy are approximate results whose EFT validity is questioned.

Doubly-subtracted fixed-u dispersion relations equate low-energy EFT residues to high-energy discontinuities expanded in spinning partial waves with Wigner d functions. Forward expansions and momentum-integrated sum rules provide different classes of constraints.

Improved integral sum rules subtract higher-derivative coefficient contributions; null constraints equate alternative representations of the same EFT coefficient. Weighted functionals in p = √(−u), optimized with SDPB, constrain the remaining low-energy coefficients.

The generalized optical theorem packages spectral densities into a positive-semidefinite helicity matrix. Spin/parity selection sectors reduce positivity tests to scalars and a two-dimensional matrix, enabling bounds on off-diagonal amplitudes through the elastic channels.
Extends the zero-charge, zero-matter exponential solution through the ansatz H = c1 exp(λkφ) + c2 exp(−λkφ), with k = √((3+α)/2) and λ written as λ(ω,ΩM); selects two integration-constant branches.
Integrates the phase equation to θ̇ = ω/(a³φ²), where ω is an integration constant. Then uses Ḣ = H′φ̇ to obtain a quadratic equation for φ̇, differentiates it, and imposes constant roll.

Compute Hall–Littlewood index contributions through representation sums, puncture branching rules, Hall–Littlewood polynomials, weighted Dynkin diagrams and the inverse Cartan matrix. The leading orders of the two spinor representations locate the first possible difference between puncture-color choices.

Augment compositing blocks with their Higgs-branch generators, including spinor chirality, and count gauge singlets in tensor products along the quiver. Some examples also require spinorial half-hypermultiplet scalars at the ends.

Combine imported misalignment-abundance estimates for radiation domination and early matter domination with CMB isocurvature constraints. Follow modulus decay chains and convert their dark-radiation energy fraction into ΔN_eff using energy and entropy degrees of freedom.

Expand the four-dimensional Kähler and scalar potentials about the LVS vacuum through cubic order, diagonalize kinetic and mass terms, and canonically normalize fields to extract trilinear decay couplings. The treatment explicitly includes vertices from expanding the kinetic terms.

Use a dilute bounce gas to extract an imaginary energy correction. The fluctuation contribution has a negative eigenvalue. Endpoint prefactor estimates borrow quoted quantum-mechanical decay-rate formulas: an inverted quartic problem near zero charge parameter and a cubic potential near saddle merger. This does not supply the general determinant function explicitly.

Use state–operator correspondence and the charge-projected partition function Z(β,Q)=Tr[e^(−βH)δ(Q̂−Q)], extracting Δ(Q)=−lim(β→∞)β^−1 log Z. Fourier projection becomes an imaginary-chemical-potential path integral with twisted boundary conditions. The associated saddle operation is only a qualified 'Legendre transformation', since the grand canonical function is not convex here.

Write ϕ₁=a e^(iχ)/√2 and eliminate χ using a²χ̇=ρ, where ρ=Q/α(D). This gives V(a)=ρ²/(2a²)+m²a²/2+ga⁴/4. The Euclidean radial bounce returns to a₀ through a turning point a₁ with V(a₁)=V(a₀). Its subtracted action is Sb=2α(D)∫[a₀,a₁] da √[2(V(a)−V(a₀))]; the general action function is evaluated numerically.

Construct embeddings by consistent scalar truncations, toroidal/KK and supersymmetry-preserving Scherk–Schwarz reductions. The generalized ANT construction dualizes an axion, reduces dimension and eliminates a top-form after adding the required total derivative.

Reduce the homogeneous field equations using a lapse choice and the Friedmann constraint; compactify the expanding phase space to an upper half unit ball. Analyze invariant boundaries, an invariant plane, monotonic flow and fixed-point linearizations.

Evolve a specified potential from a frozen initial field, select the initial value to reproduce the present abundance, and translate the resulting displacement into a coupling. The principal application fixes the axion to all dark energy.

Use an integrating factor to isolate a force-driven trajectory and a decaying initial-data transient. Applied to axion dark energy, this explains why recent displacement mainly tracks the local potential slope.

Compare rotation inferred from polarization generated at two epochs. Large-scale polarization provides reionization information, allowing an early-evolving axion explanation to be distinguished from a predominantly late-time one.

Model intrinsic polarization spectra and observational nuisances, then infer a common rotation from their E/B mixing. The paper uses published rotation estimates rather than implementing this spectral inference.

Discrete Abelian gauging uses Z_gauged = |H⁰(M;A)|/|H¹(M;A)| times the sum over H²(M;A) on closed manifolds. The Dirichlet boundary formula uses relative cohomology with one marked point per boundary component; Poincaré duality expresses it through line insertions.

Uses the reviewed MTC and Frobenius-algebra framework for anyon condensation. A network of algebra-object lines and multiplication/comultiplication morphisms is placed on edges dual to a triangulation. Generic networks are insufficient because the non-Abelian algebra object need not be transparent to itself.

Surgery and completeness relations reduce amplitudes to handlebody conformal blocks. A condensation projector implements the surviving line content and supplies an explicit factorization argument for the toroidal wormhole.

Use the long exact sequence of (X,∂X), Mayer-Vietoris sequences and elliptic monodromy to compute boundary torsion. For elliptic K3s over C with multiple discriminant points, the stated formula is h^(2) ≅ Tor coker(T−1), with T the ordered total monodromy.

Construct Lefschetz thimbles and compact rational representatives using intersection pairings and Smith normal forms of negative Cartan matrices. Coefficients descend to Q/Z; replacing fibral curves by their ruled Cartan divisors constructs Pontryagin-dual divisors.

Determine codimension-two screening through explicit resolutions or box graphs describing the relative Mori cone. Surviving divisor combinations must intersect every effective compact curve integrally; triple intersections then supply SymTFT coefficients.
Use constrained multiplets, especially X²=0, to package the Goldstino and other brane fields; superconformal supergravity and the new D-term provide supersymmetric completions.

Differentiate each term using its scaling weight, retain sign information, and test the resulting identity at a putative critical point. For scaling limits, identify sectors that cannot disappear, match their powers, and evaluate the resulting volume and coupling behavior.

Find positive stationary potentials numerically, adjust the largest negative tadpole with a classical rescaling, then check the remaining tadpoles and control parameters. Treat flux quantization and localized-source validity as additional consistency conditions.

Normalize two flux magnitudes, solve the axionic equations, eliminate anti-brane counts linearly and solve h quadratically. Scan the remaining real moduli and retain points satisfying positivity and the required isotropic or enlarged Hessian test.

Represent the dual chiral spinor as a projected derivative, insert it into the mixed field-strength density, convert the F-density to a D-density, and integrate by parts. The operator definitions and density-conversion rules are imported tensor-calculus ingredients.

Construct a Minkowski progenitor without flat directions, lower its vacuum energy to AdS, and then uplift to de Sitter. The intermediate downshift is reported to permit tuning the cosmological constant separately from the supersymmetry-breaking scale.

Promote the constrained field strength to an unconstrained chiral spinor and impose its constraint by a multiplier. Eliminate either the dual vector potential or the original spinor. The first branch imposes a Bianchi identity; the second gives a reciprocal quadratic coefficient.

Solve supersymmetry conditions D_I W=0, additionally W=0 for Minkowski progenitors, and inspect scalar mass eigenvalues. Classical de Sitter critical points are also sought numerically using Mathematica.

For the cubic momentum deformation, calculate ΔP using a Gaussian momentum-space test state and plot the equality versions of the uncertainty bounds. The displayed comparison uses β=0.01; these are lower-bound plots, not direct demonstrations that each plotted value is attained.

Evaluate operator commutators and their variance bounds, distinguishing the variance of modified momentum P from that of canonical p. Minimize the KMM lower bound and use bounded physical momentum to infer a positive lower bound on position uncertainty in capped models.

Sphere truncations turn higher-codimension brane geometries into lower-dimensional running solutions. Einstein-frame matching fixes radion normalization, and a proper-distance coordinate exposes local asymptotics. For Dp-branes the authors reexpress known solutions rather than derive them from a reduced potential.

Introduce the tunneling potential Vt=V−φ′²/2 and parameterize V=a(φ)Vt. Reduced equations determine Vt and then the scalar and warp-factor profiles, with a remaining Einstein equation checked for consistency.

Construct the short-proper-time heat kernel using Synge's world function, van Vleck determinant and coincidence limits. Derive local coefficients through transport recursions and Gilkey's operator-deformation identities.

Split fields into background and quantum pieces, fix the quantum gauge symmetry, and expand the action quadratically. One-loop Gaussian integrals become Hessian determinants; statistics and Faddeev–Popov ghosts determine determinant powers and signs.

Analytically continue ζ(s)=Σ(λ_n/μ^{d_A})^{−s}, defining log det A=−ζ′(0) in the scaled-spectrum convention. Relate ζ to the heat trace by a Mellin transform. Zeta determinants can have a multiplicative anomaly, so determinant factorization requires care.
Choose k_c as the largest comoving wavenumber whose primordial evolution is to be protected, and demand l_phys(t_b;k_c)>m_pl^−1. Trace that wavelength backward through the assumed expansion history.

Compare the cutoff-induced upper bound on inflationary e-foldings with the lower bound needed for the present Hubble scale to have been initially sub-Hubble. Use Friedmann evolution, redshift-temperature relations and alternative reheating histories to obtain energy-scale conditions.

Add covariant Robin boundary-volume terms to fix initial and final Hubble rates. The chosen TCC term has vanishing variation at these fixed boundaries and no explicit lapse dependence, allowing its exponential factor to be extracted from the q and N integrals.

Treat a tensor harmonic of fixed polarization as a time-dependent oscillator. Propagate a coherent initial state and select its mode-function coefficients by requiring recovery of the Bunch-Davies spectrum when quantum-gravity corrections are removed.

Evaluate a Lorentzian gravitational path integral semiclassically, complexifying the lapse and using Picard-Lefschetz steepest-descent contours. Fluctuation prefactors are ignored in the background saddle approximation.

Use Binet's equation and a revolving-orbit angular rescaling, expand a general central force about a nearly circular orbit, and linearize in the added force. The output isolates the combination of force and radial derivative probed by lunar perigee motion.

The proposed limit-setting procedure replaces a background-induced transition shift δEpq by QδEpq, with Q calculated for a homogeneous neutron sphere. It interpolates between unscreened and suppressed response without solving a coupled neutron–dilaton quantum problem.

Insert the scalar profile into Uφ = A2mNφ²/(2mPl²), evaluate diagonal matrix elements for level shifts, and use nondegenerate perturbation sums for state and density corrections. The one-mirror application reduces to an explicit Airy-function integral.

Integrate the autonomous field equation once, impose boundary data, approximate the potential locally, and solve the resulting quadrature. Interface continuity fixes integration constants. The paper uses this standard operation to construct new approximate mirror profiles.

Linearize separately inside and outside a homogeneous sphere, reduce the radial equations, choose regular or decaying branches, and solve two interface-matching equations. The operation produces both the near-source profile and the coefficient used to define screening.

Compute bordism using Atiyah–Hirzebruch and Adams spectral sequences, Steenrod operations, and A(1)-module decompositions. Pontrjagin–Thom multiplication identifies appropriate surviving classes with product representatives S¹ × M₈.

Construct anomaly inflow with bulk 3-form C and (d−3)-form D fields, a BF-type coupling, and a topological action Q(C). Integrating out D yields Q(Ae); boundary solutions supply a dynamical 2-form B with H = dB − Ae.

Evaluate APS η-invariants on S¹ × M₈ through η = ½ index(D₈) modulo integers. Explicit test backgrounds use HP², a Bott manifold, long-root SU(2) bundles P_G over HP², and suitable SU(2) × SU(2) bundles Q_G over S⁴ × S⁴.

The supersymmetric local potential approximation retains K and W while discarding superspace higher-derivative interactions and their feedback. The retained ansatz is K = α|X|² + β|T|² + g|T|²|X|² + ¼q|X|⁴; W remains fX + ½TX² within this approximation.

Solve the truncated flow equations ζ̇ = −2ζ − 2c₁, γ̇ = −2γ − 2c₁, β̇ = −2Nγ, and α̇ = −2N(γ + ζ). Canonically normalize the fields and study critical points and scalar-mass eigenvalues of the resulting potential.

Use a Polchinski-type exact renormalization-group equation with a supersymmetric momentum regulator and off-shell component fields. The flow of coefficients quadratic in auxiliary fields is used to infer the Kähler potential.

For N=1, the paper uses G=K+log|W|², assuming W≠0, and m₃/₂²=eᴳ. It interprets the gravitino conjecture geometrically through m₃/₂²=||W||², the norm of the superpotential section on a Kähler-Hodge scalar manifold.
